lessons.title: Renaissance
lessons.notes_html:
What the Renaissance Means

Renaissance means the rebirth of intellectual learning, art, music and culture in Europe. It lasted from the early 14th century to the late 16th century and bridged the long gap between the Middle Ages and modern civilization. During this period Europe experienced a new wave of learning in philosophy, literature, science and art.

Famous People of the Renaissance

  • Leonardo da Vinci — a famous artist of the Renaissance.
  • Raphael — a famous artist of the Renaissance.
  • William Shakespeare — a famous English writer and dramatist.

Importance of the Printing Press

  • Johannes Gutenberg put the printing press into operation in 1450.
  • It spread knowledge to other parts of the world quickly and cheaply.
  • Religious messages could now be printed and spread in the form of books, and people started to read in different languages.
  • Education became reachable for every person, so the Renaissance spread faster.

Three Things Artists Focused On

  • Painting portraits — showing real human faces and feelings.
  • The natural world — painted as it actually looked.
  • The technique of perspective — giving depth and a real-life look to paintings.

Key Dates

YearEvent
14th centuryRenaissance begins in Italy
1450Gutenberg printing press
1452Leonardo da Vinci is born
1483Raphael is born
1564William Shakespeare is born

mcqs.q: What does the word 'Renaissance' mean?
options: The rebirth of intellectual learning, art, music and culture in Europe
The birth of a new religion in Europe
A long war between European countries
The discovery of a new continent
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the rebirth of intellectual learning, art, music and culture in Europe. After the slow Middle Ages, learning in philosophy, literature, science and art came back to life. That is why this period is called a 'rebirth'.

mcqs.q: The Renaissance lasted from:
options: The early 14th century to the late 16th century
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the early 14th century to the late 16th century. The chapter states that the Renaissance began in Italy in the 14th century. It bridged the long gap between the Middle Ages and modern civilization.

mcqs.q: Who put the printing press into operation in 1450?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Johannes Gutenberg. His printing press of 1450 spread knowledge quickly and cheaply in the form of books. This made education reachable for every person and helped the Renaissance spread faster.

mcqs.q: How did the printing press help the Renaissance?
options: It printed money for the kings of Europe
It stopped people from reading religious books
It was used only for printing pictures of kings
It spread knowledge quickly and cheaply, so education reached every person
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that it spread knowledge quickly and cheaply. Religious messages could be printed as books and people began reading in different languages. As education became reachable for all, the Renaissance spread faster.

mcqs.q: Two famous artists of the Renaissance were:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Leonardo da Vinci and Raphael. The exercise names them as the two famous artists of the Renaissance. Shakespeare was a writer and dramatist, not a painter.

mcqs.q: William Shakespeare is a famous:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is an English writer and dramatist. The book's fill-in exercise states this directly. He was born in 1564, near the end of the Renaissance period.

mcqs.q: In Renaissance portrait painting, artists showed:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is real human faces and feelings. Portrait painting was one of the three things Renaissance artists focused on. It showed people as they really looked, with true expressions.

mcqs.q: The technique of perspective in painting gives:
options: Depth and a real-life look to paintings
mcqs.why: The correct answer is depth and a real-life look. Perspective was the third focus of Renaissance artists, along with portraits and the natural world. It made flat paintings look real and deep.

mcqs.q: The Renaissance bridged the long gap between:
options: The Middle Ages and modern civilization
Ancient Rome and the Middle Ages
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Middle Ages and modern civilization. The chapter says the Renaissance connected these two ages. It carried Europe from medieval ways into the modern world.

mcqs.q: Before the Renaissance, Europe faced hardships such as:
options: Shortage of food, unemployment, child labour and lack of basic necessities of life
mcqs.why: The correct answer is shortage of food, unemployment, child labour and lack of basic necessities. The textbook introduction lists these hardships of medieval Europe. Such circumstances brought drastic changes in European history.

lessons.title: Reformation and the Age of Exploration
lessons.notes_html:
Why the Reformation Occurred

The Reformation occurred because Martin Luther started a religious movement in the 16th century against the practices of the Catholic Church. It resulted in the formation of new groups within Christianity and later also developed political dimensions. It brought many social, political and cultural changes throughout Europe.

The Age of Exploration

The Age of Exploration, also known as the Age of Discovery, was the period from the 1400s to the 1600s when Europeans travelled by sea to new places to learn about them and to search for things in them. They found new sea routes to Asia, Africa and North America and developed new economic markets. They also established colonies to extend their countries overseas.

Importance of the Age of Discovery

  • It gave Europeans new sea routes, new markets and colonies in many parts of the world.
  • Vasco da Gama reached India after rounding Africa in 1498, which gave Portugal direct access to Asian markets.
  • Through trade and colonies the European countries became rich and powerful across the globe.
  • English merchants founded the East India Company in 1600.

Key Dates

YearEvent

1492Columbus lands in the Caribbean
1497John Cabot reaches North America
1498Vasco da Gama reaches India

1519Spanish explore Mexico

mcqs.q: The Reformation was a religious movement of which century?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the 16th century. Martin Luther started the movement in this century against the practices of the Catholic Church. It later also developed political dimensions.

mcqs.q: Who started the Reformation?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Martin Luther. He began the religious movement against the practices of the Catholic Church. It resulted in the formation of new groups within Christianity.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Catholic Church. Luther opposed its practices, and new groups formed within Christianity. The movement brought social, political and cultural changes throughout Europe.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Age of Discovery. Both names are used for the period from the 1400s to the 1600s. In this period Europeans travelled by sea to new places.

mcqs.q: During the Age of Exploration, Europeans travelled by sea mainly to:
options: Learn about new places and search for things in them
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to learn about new places and search for things in them. They found new sea routes to Asia, Africa and North America. They also developed new markets and established colonies overseas.

mcqs.q: Vasco da Gama reached India in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1498, after rounding Africa. His voyage gave Portugal direct access to Asian markets. This made the Age of Discovery very important for the Europeans.

mcqs.q: The East India Company was founded by:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is English merchants. The book's exercise states this directly, and the company was formed in 1600. It later became the door through which the British entered India.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1492. The chapter timeline shows Columbus landing in the Caribbean in that year. John Cabot reached North America later, in 1497.

mcqs.q: The Portuguese captured Malacca in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1511. The timeline of the Age of Exploration records the Portuguese capture of Malacca in that year. Malacca was an important trading port in Asia.

mcqs.q: Through trade and colonies, the European countries became:
options: Rich and powerful across the globe
mcqs.why: The correct answer is rich and powerful across the globe. New sea routes, markets and colonies brought wealth to Europe. That is why the Age of Discovery proved so important for the Europeans.

lessons.title: Enlightenment and the Industrial Revolution
lessons.notes_html:
What is the Enlightenment?

The Enlightenment was a smart cultural movement in Europe in the 17th and 18th centuries, also called the Age of Reason. People began to think carefully and used logic and reason to understand things, instead of following tradition blindly. It emphasized reasoning and individualism, and educated people began to apply a scientific approach to different aspects of society.

Great Thinkers

  • Jacques Rousseau — a French philosopher and writer; his Social Contract theory influenced the French Revolution.
  • Isaac Newton — a great mathematician who gave the law of universal gravitation and the laws of motion, helped create modern physics, and figured out calculus.
  • Descartes — a famous French philosopher.

Cloth Making Before and After the Industrial Revolution

  • Before: making clothes was a small-scale job done at home or on farms, called the cottage industry; it was slow and inefficient.
  • After: new machines — John Kay's and James Hargreaves' weaving and spinning machines, Arkwright's water frame, Cartwright's power loom and Eli Whitney's cotton gin — made cloth much faster in factories.
  • As factories started appearing, Britain became the first country to industrialize.

Key Dates

YearEvent
1760Industrial Revolution begins in Britain
1775American Revolution begins
1789French Revolution begins
1820-1840Industrial Revolution spreads further

mcqs.q: The Enlightenment is a:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a movement. It was a smart cultural movement in Europe in the 17th and 18th centuries. It is also called the Age of Reason.

mcqs.q: The Enlightenment is also called:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Age of Reason. People began to use logic and reason to understand things instead of following tradition blindly. It emphasized reasoning and individualism.

mcqs.q: Descartes was a famous philosopher of which country?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is France. The book's exercise states that Descartes was a famous French philosopher. Rousseau, another thinker of this age, was also French.

mcqs.q: A compass contains a:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a needle. The compass needle points to the north and helps travellers find direction. Such instruments supported the voyages and scientific thinking of the age.

mcqs.q: Jacques Rousseau's political philosophy is known for the theory of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Social Contract. Rousseau was a French philosopher and writer, and this theory influenced the French Revolution. Gravitation was Newton's contribution, not Rousseau's.

mcqs.q: Isaac Newton gave the law of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is universal gravitation. Newton also made rules about how things move, which helped create modern physics. He also figured out calculus, a tool for solving math problems.

mcqs.q: Before the Industrial Revolution, cloth making at home or on farms was called:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the cottage industry. It was small-scale, slow and inefficient work done at home or on farms. After the Industrial Revolution, machines made cloth much faster in factories.

mcqs.q: The cotton gin was invented by:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Eli Whitney. The chapter lists his cotton gin among the machines that sped up cloth production. Arkwright made the water frame and Cartwright the power loom.

mcqs.q: The first country to industrialize was:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Britain. As factories started appearing, Britain became the first country to industrialize. The Industrial Revolution began there in 1760.

mcqs.q: The Industrial Revolution began in Britain in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1760. The chapter timeline starts the Industrial Revolution in Britain at this year. It then spread further during 1820-1840.

lessons.title: Modernisation in Europe
lessons.notes_html:
How Perspectives Changed

The perspectives of the world changed because advancements in technology, art, literature, human rights and fundamental beliefs challenged the old worldviews and opinions. Inventions such as the printing press, the telescope and the steam engine, and later the computer and the internet, spread knowledge and new ideas quickly to every part of the world. In this way the world passed from traditional ways of thinking into a more scientifically advanced and technologically swift modern world.

Impacts of Technology on Our Lives

  • Communication, travel, work and learning have become much faster and easier — seen in the telephone, electricity, computers and the internet.
  • Young people spend too much time on social technologies and are becoming isolated from one another.
  • Traditional means of social gatherings are fading away.
  • A new generation has become fully reliant or dependent on these technologies.

The Internet

The internet, begun with the World Wide Web invented by Tim Berners-Lee in 1989 and made wireless by Wi-Fi in 1997, has changed our lifestyles by giving us instant information, education, work and communication at any place and time. People now stay connected with family and friends across the world and do many daily tasks online instead of in person.

Evolution of Computers

YearEvent
1703Leibniz binary system
1971First microprocessor
1981IBM personal computer
1991Linus Torvalds created Linux

mcqs.q: Belief is a:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a state of mind. The chapter's exercise states this directly. Beliefs are part of the worldviews and opinions that changed as the world became modern.

mcqs.q: Digital technology helps to pass:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is information. Digital technology passes information quickly to every part of the world. This is one way technology changed perspectives and made the world modern.

mcqs.q: The World Wide Web was invented by:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Tim Berners-Lee. He invented the World Wide Web in 1989, with which the internet began. Linus Torvalds created Linux in 1991.

mcqs.q: The internet was made wireless by Wi-Fi in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1997. The chapter states that Wi-Fi made the internet wireless in that year. The World Wide Web itself had been invented earlier, in 1989.

mcqs.q: The first microprocessor was made in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1971. The chapter's timeline of the evolution of computers gives this year for the first microprocessor. The IBM personal computer followed in 1981.

mcqs.q: The IBM personal computer came in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1981. It is listed in the timeline of the evolution of computers. The first microprocessor had already appeared ten years earlier, in 1971.

mcqs.q: Linux was created by:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Linus Torvalds. He created Linux in 1991, as the chapter timeline shows. Leibniz is linked with the binary system of 1703.

mcqs.q: One negative impact of technology given in the chapter is:
options: Young people spend too much time on social technologies and become isolated
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that young people become isolated through too much use of social technologies. The chapter lists this among the new challenges of technology. Faster communication and easier travel are positive impacts, not negative ones.

mcqs.q: Leibniz is linked in the timeline with:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the binary system in 1703. The evolution-of-computers timeline begins with Leibniz's binary system. The microprocessor came much later, in 1971.

mcqs.q: The world passed into a modern world mainly because advancements challenged old worldviews in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is technology, art and literature. The chapter says these advancements, along with human rights and beliefs, changed perspectives. Inventions spread new ideas quickly to every part of the world.

lessons.title: The British Rule in India (1600-1885)
lessons.notes_html:
Coming of the East India Company

  • Queen Elizabeth-I granted a Royal Charter to the East India Company on December 31, 1600.
  • Tipu Sultan, known as the Tiger of Mysore, was born at Devanhalli.
  • Sir Syed Ahmed Khan established a school in Aligarh in 1875.

Wars Against the British

The Indians fought many wars against the British, and the chapter lists sixteen major wars and campaigns between 1686 and 1920. These include the Carnatic Wars, the Anglo-Mysore Wars, the Anglo-Maratha Wars, the Anglo-Nepalese War and the War of Independence of 1857. Rulers such as Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan of Mysore also resisted the British bravely in southern India.

Reasons for the Failure of the War of Independence 1857

  • There was a lack of unity between Hindus and Muslims.
  • The revolt was uncoordinated and lacked strategic planning and proper leadership.
  • The British army was strong, well trained and equipped with the latest weapons.
  • Some loyal states in India also supported the British.

The Indian National Congress

The Indian National Congress, established in 1885 by a retired British officer, Allan Octavian Hume, gave the people of India a common political forum to represent their views before the British government. Its major purpose was to introduce a democratic system in India, and through it Indians began to be given a say in political affairs. In this way it spread political awareness among the people and turned scattered discontent against British rule into an organized political movement.

Key Dates

YearEvent
1600East India Company was established
1757Battle of Plassey took place
1857The War of Independence took place
1858Crown takes control of India

mcqs.q: The Royal Charter to the East India Company was granted on:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is December 31, 1600. Queen Elizabeth-I granted the charter on this date. The company then began its trade with India, which later turned into rule.

mcqs.q: Who granted the Royal Charter to the East India Company?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Queen Elizabeth-I. She granted the Royal Charter on December 31, 1600. A. O. Hume belongs to a much later event, the founding of Congress in 1885.

mcqs.q: Tipu Sultan was born at:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Devanhalli. The book's exercise states this directly. Tipu Sultan is also known as the Tiger of Mysore.

mcqs.q: Who was known as the Tiger of Mysore?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Tipu Sultan. The exercise gives him this title. He and his father Hyder Ali resisted the British bravely in southern India.

mcqs.q: Sir Syed Ahmed Khan established a school in Aligarh in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1875. The book states that he established the school in Aligarh in that year. The Indian National Congress was founded later, in 1885.

mcqs.q: How many major wars and campaigns against the British does the chapter list between 1686 and 1920?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is sixteen. They include the Carnatic Wars, the Anglo-Mysore Wars, the Anglo-Maratha Wars and the Anglo-Nepalese War. The War of Independence of 1857 is also among them.

mcqs.q: The Battle of Plassey took place in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1757. The chapter timeline places the Battle of Plassey in this year. The War of Independence came a hundred years later, in 1857.

mcqs.q: The War of Independence took place in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1857. It was the great revolt against British rule. After its failure, the Crown took direct control of India in 1858.

mcqs.q: One main reason for the failure of the War of Independence was:
options: Lack of unity between Hindus and Muslims
The weakness of the British army
Help of loyal states to the rebels
Strong central leadership of the revolt
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the lack of unity between Hindus and Muslims. The revolt was also uncoordinated and lacked planning and leadership. In fact, some loyal states supported the British, which made failure certain.

mcqs.q: The Indian National Congress was established in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1885. It gave the people of India a common political forum. Sir Syed's Aligarh school (1875) and the Muslim League (1906) belong to other years.

mcqs.q: The Indian National Congress was established by:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Allan Octavian Hume. He was a retired British officer who founded Congress in 1885. Its major purpose was to introduce a democratic system in India.

mcqs.q: After the War of Independence, the Crown took control of India in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1858. The chapter timeline shows the Crown taking control in this year. Rule by the East India Company thus came to an end.

mcqs.q: Which of these wars is listed in the chapter among the wars against the British?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Anglo-Maratha Wars. The chapter lists them with the Carnatic, Anglo-Mysore and Anglo-Nepalese wars. The First World War is not part of this list of sixteen wars.

mcqs.q: The major purpose of the Indian National Congress was to:
options: Introduce a democratic system in India
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to introduce a democratic system in India. Through Congress, Indians began to be given a say in political affairs. It turned scattered discontent into an organized political movement.

mcqs.q: Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan resisted the British bravely in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is southern India. They were rulers of Mysore in the south. Their Anglo-Mysore Wars are among the major wars listed in the chapter.

lessons.title: Self-Rule in India and Muslim Struggle (1905-1932)
lessons.notes_html:
Partition of Bengal and the Lucknow Pact

  • The partition of Bengal (1905) proved that there was Hindu dominance in the Congress.
  • The Lucknow Pact was signed in 1916 so that Congress and the Muslim League could work together and present common demands for self-rule; Congress accepted separate electorates for the Muslims.
  • The pact failed because this unity did not last long and Congress later went back on the agreed principles.

Jallianwala Bagh and the Reforms

  • The Jallianwala Bagh massacre of 1919 is also known as the Amritsar massacre; evidence shows it was planned — General Dyer blocked the only narrow exit and ordered firing on the unarmed crowd without warning.
  • The British introduced diarchy in the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms in 1919.
  • The Simon Commission came to India in 1927 to investigate the future Indian needs.

Why the Khilafat Movement Failed

  • The Turks themselves abolished the Khilafat in 1924, so the cause no longer existed.
  • Gandhi called off the Non-Cooperation Movement after the Chauri Chaura incident of 1922, which weakened the struggle.
  • Hindu-Muslim unity broke down and the movement ended without achieving its aims.

Jinnah's Fourteen Points (1929)

Jinnah's Fourteen Points were a charter of demands to protect the political, religious and cultural rights of the Muslims of India. They demanded, among other things, separate electorates, one-third Muslim representation in the central legislature, provincial autonomy and the separation of Sindh from Bombay. These points became the basis of all future Muslim demands and finally led the Muslims towards the demand for a separate homeland.

Key Dates

YearEvent
1905Partition of Bengal
1906All-India Muslim League is formed
1916Lucknow Pact is signed
1919Khilafat Movement and Jallianwala Bagh massacre
1928Nehru Report is presented

mcqs.q: The Partition of Bengal took place in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1905. The chapter timeline begins the Muslim struggle period with this event. The Muslim League was formed the next year, in 1906.

mcqs.q: The All-India Muslim League was formed in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1906. The timeline shows the League formed a year after the Partition of Bengal. It became the political party of the Muslims of India.

mcqs.q: The partition of Bengal proved that there was ______ dominance in the Congress.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Hindu dominance. The book's fill-in exercise states this directly. This realization pushed the Muslims to organize themselves politically.

mcqs.q: The Lucknow Pact was signed in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1916. Through it, Congress and the Muslim League agreed to work together for self-rule. Congress accepted separate electorates for the Muslims in this pact.

mcqs.q: In the Lucknow Pact, the Congress accepted:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is separate electorates for the Muslims. This was the great achievement of the pact of 1916. Diarchy came later, through the reforms of 1919.

mcqs.q: Diarchy was introduced in India through:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms of 1919. The book's exercise states this directly. Diarchy divided provincial subjects between elected ministers and officials.

mcqs.q: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre is also known as:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Amritsar massacre. It happened in 1919 at Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar. General Dyer ordered firing on an unarmed and peaceful crowd.

mcqs.q: Who ordered the firing at Jallianwala Bagh?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is General Dyer. He blocked the only narrow exit of the bagh and ordered firing without any warning. The firing continued until the ammunition was nearly finished.

mcqs.q: The Khilafat was abolished by the Turks in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1924. Because the Turks themselves abolished it, the cause of the Khilafat Movement no longer existed. This was the main reason for the movement's failure.

mcqs.q: Gandhi called off the Non-Cooperation Movement after:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Chauri Chaura incident of 1922. This step weakened the Khilafat struggle. Hindu-Muslim unity then broke down and the movement ended.

mcqs.q: The Simon Commission came to India in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1927. It came to investigate the future needs of India. The Nehru Report followed in 1928.

mcqs.q: The Nehru Report was presented in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1928. The chapter timeline places it between the Simon Commission (1927) and the Fourteen Points (1929). Jinnah replied to it with his Fourteen Points.

mcqs.q: Jinnah presented his Fourteen Points in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1929. They were a charter of demands to protect the rights of the Muslims of India. They became the basis of all future Muslim demands.

mcqs.q: One demand of the Fourteen Points was:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the separation of Sindh from Bombay. The Points also demanded separate electorates, one-third Muslim representation in the central legislature and provincial autonomy. They protected the political, religious and cultural rights of Muslims.

mcqs.q: After World War I, instead of self-government, Indians received:
options: The Rowlatt Act and the Jallianwala Bagh tragedy
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Rowlatt Act and the Jallianwala Bagh tragedy. Indians had supported Britain in the war and expected self-government in return. This betrayal created anger all over India and started new struggle movements.

lessons.title: Self Rule in India and Creation of Pakistan (1930-1947)
lessons.notes_html:
Simla Deputation (1906)

The Simla Deputation demanded separate electorates for the Muslims, representation in proportion to their population and political importance, and Muslim representation in councils, services and universities. Its importance is that the Viceroy accepted these demands, separate electorates were granted in the reforms of 1909, and the deputation led directly to the formation of the All-India Muslim League in 1906.

Cripps Mission and the Congress

  • The British government sent Sir Stafford Cripps with the Cripps proposals in 1942.
  • Gandhi rejected them and described them as a post-dated cheque on a crashing bank, because they promised self-government only after the war.
  • Quaid-i-Azam strictly opposed the Quit India movement.
  • Gandhi had shunted the C.R. formula.
  • Wavell announced the failure of the Simla Conference.
  • The All-India Muslim League was the sole representative of the Muslims.
  • Liaquat Ali Khan presented a poor man's budget.

Why the Round Table Conferences Failed

The Round Table Conferences of 1930 to 1932 failed because the parties could not agree on the communal problem and the future constitution of India. The Congress boycotted the first conference, Gandhi showed a rigid attitude in the second, and the Congress was absent from the third conference.

Why the Muslims Demanded a Separate Homeland

During the Congress rule of 1937 to 1939 the Muslims faced discrimination, injustice and attacks on their religion, language and culture. Urdu was replaced by Hindi, Bande Mataram was imposed and communal riots made the Muslims feel insecure in a united India. They therefore concluded, under the Two-Nation Theory, that as a separate nation they could only protect their rights in their own homeland.

The 3rd June Plan

The 3rd June Plan of 1947, announced by Lord Mountbatten, was very effective for the creation of Pakistan because it was accepted by both the Congress and the Muslim League and fixed a clear method and date for the transfer of power. As a result, Pakistan came into being on 14 August 1947.

Key Dates

YearEvent
1930Iqbal presents the Allahabad Address
1940Lahore Resolution is passed
1942Cripps Mission and Quit India Movement
1945-46Muslim League wins the elections
1946Cabinet Mission Plan is presented
19473rd June Plan is announced
14 August 1947Pakistan is created

mcqs.q: The Cripps Mission came to India in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1942. The British government sent Sir Stafford Cripps with the proposals in that year. The Quit India Movement also began in 1942.

mcqs.q: Who was sent to India with the Cripps proposals?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Sir Stafford Cripps. The book's exercise states this directly. Gandhi rejected his proposals as a post-dated cheque on a crashing bank.

mcqs.q: Gandhi described the Cripps proposals as:
options: A post-dated cheque on a crashing bank
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a post-dated cheque on a crashing bank. The proposals promised self-government only after the war and gave no real power immediately. For this reason Congress refused to accept them.

mcqs.q: The sole representative of the Muslims was:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the All-India Muslim League. The book states this directly. Its victory in the 1945-46 elections proved this claim.

mcqs.q: The poor man's budget was presented by:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Liaquat Ali Khan. The book's exercise records this fact. He presented it as finance member in the interim government.

mcqs.q: Who announced the failure of the Simla Conference?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Wavell. The book states that Wavell announced the failure of the Simla Conference. Mountbatten came later and announced the 3rd June Plan.

mcqs.q: Quaid-i-Azam strictly opposed which movement?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Quit India movement. The book's exercise states this directly. He considered it harmful for the Muslim cause at that time.

mcqs.q: Gandhi had shunted which formula?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the C.R. formula. The book's fill-in exercise records this. The Fourteen Points were Jinnah's demands, not a formula shunted by Gandhi.

mcqs.q: The Simla Deputation met the Viceroy in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1906. It demanded separate electorates and due representation for the Muslims. It led directly to the formation of the All-India Muslim League the same year.

mcqs.q: Separate electorates for Muslims were granted in the reforms of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1909. The Viceroy accepted the Simla Deputation's demands, and they were granted in these reforms. Diarchy came later, in the reforms of 1919.

mcqs.q: The Lahore Resolution was passed in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1940. The chapter timeline places it between the Allahabad Address (1930) and the Cripps Mission (1942). Through it the Muslims formally demanded separate homelands.

mcqs.q: The Cabinet Mission Plan was presented in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1946. The timeline shows it after the Muslim League's election victory of 1945-46. The 3rd June Plan followed in 1947.

mcqs.q: The 3rd June Plan was announced by:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Lord Mountbatten. The plan fixed a clear method and date for the transfer of power. It was accepted by both Congress and the Muslim League.

mcqs.q: Pakistan came into being on:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 14 August 1947. Power was transferred within 72 days of the announcement of the 3rd June Plan. The Lahore Resolution had been passed earlier, on 23 March 1940.

mcqs.q: The Muslims demanded a separate homeland under:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Two-Nation Theory. The chapter says the Muslims are a nation according to any definition of the nation. After the Congress rule of 1937-39, they concluded they could protect their rights only in their own homeland.

lessons.title: Development and Sustainable Development
lessons.notes_html:
The Industrial Revolution and Change

The Industrial Revolution was the major change that began in the second half of the 18th century, when mostly rural societies in Europe and America were transformed into industrialized urban areas. It passed through stages that used water and steam power, then electric power for mass production, then electronics and information technology, and now artificial intelligence and robotics. It increased wealth, production of goods and the standard of living, but it also caused pollution, overpopulation and deforestation.

Sustainable Development

  • Sustainable development is around four components: climate change, nutrient cycles, hydrological cycle and biodiversity.
  • Development must keep all four components in balance, so that resources remain safe for future generations.
  • Fishing and forestry can be sustained by safeguarding natural resources, fixing catch limits, stopping fishing in the breeding season and planting more trees than are cut.

Organizations Working for Development

  • UNO works for the sectors of education, health, social justice and environment.
  • UNODC — the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime — works in the sector of drugs and crime.
  • NDMA stands for National Disaster Management Authority, the national body that works to prevent disasters, prepare for them and reduce their impact.

Major Issues Impacting the Land and People

These include global warming, ineffective governance, wasteful food practices, loss of biodiversity, plastic pollution, deforestation, air pollution, melting ice caps with rising sea levels, ocean acidification, use of fertilizers and pesticides, land exhaustion and unanalysed carbon emissions.

Coastal Areas of Pakistan

Pakistan's coastal areas are divided into five parts: the Gwadar Coast, Lasbela Coast, Karachi Coast, Thatta Coast from Korangi Creek up to the Indian border at Sir Creek, and the Rann of Kutch from Badin to Tharparkar districts.

Activity

Survey some common items in your home and find out where each item was made or produced. Note how many items are made in Pakistan (usually most household items such as towels, furniture and utensils) and how many come from other countries (usually electronic items such as computers and mobile phones, which reach us through international trade).

mcqs.q: In the second half of the 18th century, rural societies in Europe and America changed into:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is industrialized urban areas. The Industrial Revolution transformed mostly rural societies in Europe and America. Agrarian societies changed because of this revolution.

mcqs.q: Sustainable development is around how many components?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is four components. They are climate change, nutrient cycles, hydrological cycle and biodiversity. Development must keep all of them in balance.

mcqs.q: Which of these is one of the four components of sustainable development?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is biodiversity. Together with climate change, nutrient cycles and the hydrological cycle, it forms the four components. Resources must remain safe for future generations.

mcqs.q: NDMA stands for:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is National Disaster Management Authority. It is the national body backed by the government. It works to prevent disasters, prepare for them and reduce their impact.

mcqs.q: UNODC works in the sector of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is drugs and crime. Its full name, the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime, shows its field. The UNO itself works in education, health, social justice and environment.

mcqs.q: The UNO works for which sectors?
options: Education, health, social justice and environment
mcqs.why: The correct answer is education, health, social justice and environment. The book explains that international organizations work for these sectors in Pakistan and globally. Their aim is to improve the quality of life of people.

mcqs.q: Pakistan's coastal areas are divided into how many parts?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is five parts. They are the Gwadar Coast, Lasbela Coast, Karachi Coast, Thatta Coast and the Rann of Kutch. The Thatta Coast runs from Korangi Creek to Sir Creek.

mcqs.q: Which coast runs from Korangi Creek up to Sir Creek?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Thatta Coast. The chapter describes it as running from Korangi Creek to the Indian border at Sir Creek. The Rann of Kutch extends from Badin to Tharparkar.

mcqs.q: One way to sustain fishing is:
options: Catching as many fish as possible
Fixing catch limits and stopping fishing in the breeding season
Using finer nets for small fish
mcqs.why: The correct answer is fixing catch limits and stopping fishing in the breeding season. These ways let fish keep renewing themselves. Safeguarding natural resources is the principle given in the chapter.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a major issue impacting the land and people?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is plastic pollution and deforestation. Other issues are global warming, loss of biodiversity, air pollution and melting ice caps. These damage natural resources and make life difficult for people.

lessons.title: Global Warming and Climate Change
lessons.notes_html:
The Greenhouse Effect

The greenhouse effect is the warming of the Earth when carbon dioxide and other pollutants, along with greenhouse gases, gather in the atmosphere. These gases absorb sunlight and solar radiation that would have bounced off the Earth's surface and escaped into space. The pollutants stay in the atmosphere for a long time, trapping heat and making the Earth warmer.

How Humans Influence Climate Change

  • Increased consumption of coal, oil and natural gas raises the concentration of greenhouse gases in the air.
  • Industrialization has increased cars, planes, power stations, factories and processing plants, which release more pollution.
  • As a result the climate faces more floods, droughts, hurricanes and extreme weather events.

Key Facts from the Chapter

  • Infrared radiation is a type of electromagnetic radiation with longer wavelengths than visible light.
  • Cuba, the USA and China are badly hit by deadly hurricanes; the strongest US hurricane of 1935 was the Labor Day Hurricane.
  • Ethiopia is one of the largest humanitarian aid beneficiaries in the world; about three million people there are affected by crop failures each year.
  • The 2010 floods in Pakistan affected 10 million children.
  • IDPs means internally displaced persons — people forced to leave their homes who stay within their own country, such as the people of Malakand Division and FATA in 2008.

Developed and Underdeveloped Countries

United Kingdom (developed)Ethiopia (underdeveloped)
Farmers adapt farming practices to improve soil water retentionFarmers divide land into smaller plots and sow different crops
Management strategies reduce the impact of droughtCrop rotation with leguminous crops restores soil fertility

Activity

With the help of the internet, find out which countries have been affected by natural disasters in the current decade, such as Pakistan (floods), Turkey and Syria (earthquake) and the USA (hurricanes). Note that poor countries suffer more because they are less prepared.

mcqs.q: The greenhouse effect is:
options: The cooling of the Earth by ice caps
The growing of plants in glass houses
The reflection of all sunlight back into space
The warming of the Earth when greenhouse gases gather in the atmosphere and trap heat
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the warming of the Earth as gases trap heat. Carbon dioxide and other pollutants absorb radiation that would have escaped into space. They stay in the atmosphere for a long time and make the Earth warmer.

mcqs.q: Human activities increase climate change mainly through:
options: Increased consumption of coal, oil and natural gas
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the increased consumption of coal, oil and natural gas. This raises the concentration of greenhouse gases in the air. Industrialization also adds pollution through cars, planes and power stations.

mcqs.q: Infrared radiation has wavelengths that are:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is longer than visible light. That is why infrared radiation is invisible to the human eye. The Earth's surface emits it after being warmed by the sun.

mcqs.q: The strongest hurricane to hit the US in 1935 was called:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Labor Day Hurricane. The book states it was the most powerful hurricane to hit the US. Warmer ocean waters make hurricanes more powerful.

mcqs.q: Which three countries are badly hit by deadly hurricanes?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Cuba, the USA and China. The chapter names these three countries for destructive hurricanes. The USA faced the Labor Day Hurricane in 1935.

mcqs.q: The 2010 floods in Pakistan affected how many children?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 10 million children. The floods were one of the worst disasters in the country. Children suffered through displacement, disease and loss of schooling.

mcqs.q: Ethiopia is one of the largest ______ in the world.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is humanitarian aid beneficiaries. Millions of Ethiopians receive support every year. Climate-induced droughts and crop failures repeatedly affect the country.

mcqs.q: IDPs are people who:
options: Are forced to leave their homes but stay within their own country
mcqs.why: The correct answer is people displaced inside their own country. In Pakistan in 2008, many people in Malakand Division and FATA became IDPs due to fierce fighting. They did not cross into another country.

mcqs.q: In Ethiopia, farmers restore soil fertility by:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is crop rotation with leguminous crops. Ethiopian farmers also divide land into smaller plots and sow different crops. They face climate-induced droughts affecting about three million people each year.

mcqs.q: UK farmers make their land less vulnerable to water shortages by:
options: Adapting farming practices to improve soil water retention
mcqs.why: The correct answer is adapting farming to improve soil water retention. The UK is the developed country in the comparison. Ethiopia is the underdeveloped country in the same comparison.

lessons.title: Scarcity of Water and Food Insecurity
lessons.notes_html:
Increasing Access to Safe Drinking Water

  • Build proper toilets and latrines that do not pollute water sources, because sewage is the main reason for water contamination.
  • Teach people good hygiene habits through education, so that water sources stay clean.
  • Collect and save rainwater in tanks and reservoirs for drinking, or for filling up underground water stores.

Why Water Is Contaminated in Cities Like Karachi

Many water supplies are contaminated because sewage, which includes human waste, gets into drinking water sources. Harmful chemicals from factories and the pesticides and fertilizers used in farming also end up in water bodies. In crowded cities, leaking sewerage lines mix with water supply lines and make the water unsafe to drink.

Increasing Food Production

  • Develop crop varieties that endure tough conditions, such as rice that can handle salt and sorghums and millets that can withstand drought.
  • Recycle nutrients in the soil by rotating crops.
  • Use genetic resistance in plants against pests and diseases.
  • Encourage mechanization in agriculture and introduce climate-friendly crops.

Uneven Distribution of Food

The unequal sharing of food between wealthy and impoverished nations is due to the uneven distribution of resources. In many poor countries, families spend as much as 80% of their income on food, so if prices increase twofold, these families cannot afford food anymore.

Access to Clean Water — Figures from the Chapter

PlaceFigure
PakistanOnly 20% of the population has access to clean water (survey report 2018)
IndiaAround 50% of the population has no access to safe drinking water
Mozambique45% of the population has no access to water for basic needs
Nigeria (Niger area)Only 17% has access to safe drinking water
Papua New Guinea51% drink water from ponds, lakes, rivers, swamps and springs

mcqs.q: According to the survey report of 2018, what percentage of Pakistan's population has access to clean water?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 20%. The chapter states that the largest percentage of people in Pakistan cannot access clean water. This makes water scarcity a serious problem in the country.

mcqs.q: The main reason for water contamination is:
options: Sewage getting into drinking water sources
mcqs.why: The correct answer is sewage getting into water sources. Sewage includes human waste, and leaking sewerage lines mix with supply lines in crowded cities. Factory chemicals and farm pesticides add to the pollution.

mcqs.q: One strategy to increase access to safe drinking water is:
options: Collecting and saving rainwater in tanks and reservoirs
mcqs.why: The correct answer is collecting and saving rainwater. It can be used for drinking or for filling underground water stores. Building proper toilets that do not pollute water is the other strategy in the chapter.

mcqs.q: Around what percentage of India's population has no access to safe drinking water?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is around 50%. The chapter states India has the highest number of people without clean water in the world. Pakistan's clean-water access figure is 20%, a different statistic.

mcqs.q: In Mozambique, what percentage of the population has no access to water for basic needs?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 45%. The chapter also notes that most of the country does not have access to its own toilet. Nigeria's safe-water figure, 17%, is even lower.

mcqs.q: In Nigeria, only ______ of the population has access to safe drinking water.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 17%. This very low percentage is given in the chapter for the Niger area. Most people there depend on unsafe water sources.

mcqs.q: In Papua New Guinea, 51% of the population drinks water from:
options: Ponds, lakes, rivers, swamps and springs
mcqs.why: The correct answer is ponds, lakes, rivers, swamps and springs. The chapter uses this to show how limited safe water access is there. Such sources are usually unsafe without treatment.

mcqs.q: Food production can be increased by developing crop varieties that:
options: Can handle salt and withstand drought
mcqs.why: The correct answer is varieties that handle salt and withstand drought. The chapter gives salt-tolerant rice and drought-resistant sorghums and millets as examples. Crop rotation and mechanization are other strategies.

mcqs.q: In many poor countries, families spend as much as ______ of their income on food.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 80%. So if food prices increase twofold, these families cannot afford food anymore. This is how uneven distribution of food causes food shortage.

mcqs.q: Water supplies in Karachi are contaminated because:
options: There is no rainfall in the city
The sea water is too salty
Leaking sewerage lines mix with water supply lines
People boil the water too much
mcqs.why: The correct answer is leaking sewerage lines mixing with supply lines. Sewage and human waste enter the drinking water sources. Harmful chemicals from factories also end up in water bodies.

lessons.title: Interdependence
lessons.notes_html:
Why Interdependence Is Needed

Interdependence is needed because no individual and no country can fulfil all of its needs alone. Some countries are rich in natural resources while others are specialized in technology, and many countries depend on others for labour force and trade routes. Therefore, people and countries depend on each other for food, goods, services and a good life, and globalization has made the world connected and interdependent.

Global Cooperation in Disasters

Countries and international organizations help affected people together. The UN and other organizations provide relief, rehabilitation, food, shelter and medical help in disaster-hit areas. A big disaster in one country becomes the concern of the whole world.

The Oil Crisis After 1970

After 1970, oil prices went up a lot. Two huge events in the Middle East — the Yom Kippur War in 1973 and the Iranian Revolution in 1979 — made oil from that area scarce. Countries that needed oil, such as Canada, Australia, New Zealand, the United States, Western Europe and Japan, did not have enough oil, so its prices rose greatly.

People and Organizations That Help Others

  • Mother Teresa, a Catholic nun, helped poor and sick people in Kolkata, India; she won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979.
  • The UN, started in 1945 with 193 member countries, keeps peace, protects rights and helps in emergencies; since the 1990s it helped end fights in Sierra Leone, Liberia, Burundi, Sudan and Nepal.
  • WFP stands for World Food Programme; it received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2020.
  • Greenpeace is a non-governmental environmental organization, started in 1971, with its main office in Amsterdam, Netherlands.
  • The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2020 was awarded to Harvey J. Alter, Michael Houghton and Charles M. Rice for finding the Hepatitis C virus.
  • In 1979, Sheldon Lee Glashow, Abdus Salam and Steven Weinberg received the Nobel Prize in Physics.

mcqs.q: Interdependence is needed because:
options: Countries should not trade at all
No individual and no country can fulfil all of its needs alone
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that no country can fulfil all its needs alone. Some countries are rich in natural resources and others in technology. Globalization has made the world connected and interdependent.

mcqs.q: Oil prices rose greatly after 1970 because of:
options: The Yom Kippur War (1973) and the Iranian Revolution (1979)
The discovery of oil in America
The end of the United Nations
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the two Middle East events of 1973 and 1979. They made oil from that area scarce. Oil-needing countries such as the USA, Japan and Western Europe then faced high prices.

mcqs.q: Mother Teresa won the Nobel Peace Prize in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1979. She was a Catholic nun who devoted her life to poor and sick people in Kolkata, India. She later became a saint in the Catholic Church.

mcqs.q: WFP stands for:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is World Food Programme. It is the food-assistance organization of the United Nations. It received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2020 for helping to stop hunger.

mcqs.q: The World Food Programme received the Nobel Peace Prize in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 2020. It was honoured for its efforts to stop hunger and to prevent hunger being used as a weapon in wars. Mother Teresa's Peace Prize was much earlier, in 1979.

mcqs.q: Greenpeace is a:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a non-governmental environmental organization. It started in 1971 and has its main office in Amsterdam. It is not part of any government.

mcqs.q: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2020 was awarded for finding:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Hepatitis C virus. Harvey J. Alter, Michael Houghton and Charles M. Rice received the prize. The chapter records this as an example of science serving humanity.

mcqs.q: Abdus Salam received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1979 together with:
options: Sheldon Lee Glashow and Steven Weinberg
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Glashow and Weinberg. They were honoured for helping us understand how tiny particles interact. The Medicine prize winners of 2020 are a different group.

mcqs.q: The United Nations was started in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1945. The UN helps countries by keeping peace, protecting rights and helping in emergencies. It has helped end fights in Sierra Leone, Liberia, Burundi, Sudan and Nepal since the 1990s.

mcqs.q: How can an individual help people in other places?
options: By wise consumer choices, petitions, letters and joining relief activities
mcqs.why: The correct answer is through personal actions such as wise consumer choices and supporting welfare organizations. Even small actions in one place can improve life elsewhere. This is the practical side of interdependence.

lessons.title: The World of Air
lessons.notes_html:
What Air Is Made Up Of

Air is made up of a mixture of different gases like oxygen and nitrogen. Nitrogen is the most abundant gas and makes up 78% of the gases in the atmosphere, while oxygen and small amounts of other gases such as argon and carbon dioxide are also present. This mixture surrounds the Earth, and living things live and breathe in it. The atmosphere is the thin layer of air that surrounds Earth.

The Four Layers of the Atmosphere

LayerFeatures
Troposphere0-10 km, nearest to the surface of the Earth
Stratosphere10-30 km, consists of ozone layers
Mesosphere30-50 km
Thermosphere50-400 km, top layer where the air is hot but very thin

Above them, about 400 km above the Earth's surface, begins the exosphere.

Winds and Their Measurement

  • Trade winds are regular winds, also called tropical easterlies, blowing from high-pressure areas near the tropics towards the low-pressure area near the equator — northeast trades in the Northern Hemisphere and southeast trades in the Southern Hemisphere.
  • Surface winds blow close to the Earth's surface and are slowed down by friction; surface wind is measured at a height of 10 meters above the ground.
  • A wind vane shows the direction of the wind; an anemometer measures the speed of the wind.
  • In a cyclone in the Southern Hemisphere, the wind moves in a clockwise direction (counterclockwise in the Northern Hemisphere).
  • Most tornadoes form from thunderstorms.
  • Pressure decreases rapidly with altitude because the air becomes less dense.
  • Earth's seasons change because, as Earth revolves around the Sun, its tilt gives one hemisphere more direct rays of the Sun.

mcqs.q: The most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere, making up 78% of the gases, is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is nitrogen. It makes up 78% of the gases in the atmosphere. Oxygen and small amounts of argon and carbon dioxide make up the rest.

mcqs.q: The thin layer of air that surrounds Earth is called:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the atmosphere. Living things live and breathe in this mixture of gases. It is divided into layers such as the troposphere and stratosphere.

mcqs.q: The layer of the atmosphere nearest to the surface of the Earth is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the troposphere. It extends from 0 to about 10 km above the surface. The stratosphere, with its ozone layers, lies above it.

mcqs.q: The ozone layers are found in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the stratosphere. The chapter places the ozone layers in this second layer, 10-30 km up. The thermosphere is the top layer, where air is hot but very thin.

mcqs.q: Surface wind is measured at a height of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 10 meters above the ground. Surface winds blow close to the surface and are slowed by friction. An anemometer measures their speed and a wind vane their direction.

mcqs.q: An anemometer is used to measure:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the speed of the wind. A wind vane, in contrast, shows the direction from which the wind is blowing. Both instruments are used together to study weather.

mcqs.q: In a cyclone in the Southern Hemisphere, the wind moves:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is clockwise. A cyclone spins counterclockwise in the Northern Hemisphere, so in the Southern Hemisphere the direction is opposite. A cyclone forms around a centre of low pressure.

mcqs.q: Most tornadoes form from:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is thunderstorms. The chapter's exercise gives this directly. Tornadoes are violent spinning winds that develop out of strong thunderstorms.

mcqs.q: Pressure decreases rapidly with altitude because the air becomes:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is less dense. As we go higher, there is less air above to press down. That is why pressure falls rapidly with altitude.

mcqs.q: The basic reason for Earth's seasons is that:
options: The Sun moves away from Earth
As Earth revolves around the Sun, Earth's tilt gives one hemisphere more direct rays of the Sun
The Moon blocks the Sun's rays
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Earth's tilt during its revolution around the Sun. The hemisphere tilted towards the Sun gets more direct rays and has summer. The other hemisphere has winter at the same time.

lessons.title: Urbanization and Internal Migration
lessons.notes_html:
The Process of Urbanization

Urbanization is a continuous process in which more and more people migrate from rural and sub-urban areas to urban cities and permanently settle there. The process is higher where there are more economic opportunities, and both push factors and pull factors play a vital role in it. As a result, small towns grow into big cities, metropolitan cities and a metropolis, and the population, area, structures and economic activity of the place increase.

Push and Pull Factors

  • Push factors force people to leave rural areas: poverty, unavailability of jobs, security issues, tribal clashes, water shortage and droughts, and problems of education and health.
  • Pull factors attract people to cities: economic opportunities, better jobs, business and better services.
  • Social push factors can include ethnic, religious, racial and cultural persecution.
  • The major factors influencing movement of people are environmental, economic, social and political, and ecological factors.
  • Mountainous high land like the Himalayas has low population density, while flat land like the Indus Valley has high density.

Problems of Urban Cities and Their Solutions

ProblemSolution
Shanty settlementsProper city planning and low-cost housing
Traffic jamsBetter public transport and road planning
PollutionControlling factory smoke and vehicle emissions
Pressure on health and educationEnough schools and hospitals according to population
Shortage of resources and cleanlinessClean water supply and waste management

Impact of Road Networks

Road networks connect cities with villages and other cities, so people can travel easily for jobs, education, trade and medical help. Better roads increase business and economic activity. However, building roads also changes natural land and increases traffic, noise and air pollution.

mcqs.q: Urbanization is the process in which people tend to:
options: Migrate to urban cities and permanently settle there
mcqs.why: The correct answer is migrate to urban cities and settle there permanently. Small towns then grow into big cities and a metropolis. Both push and pull factors play a vital role in this process.

mcqs.q: Social push factors can include:
options: Ethnic, religious, racial and cultural persecution
mcqs.why: The correct answer is ethnic, religious, racial and cultural persecution. Such discrimination forces people to leave their home areas. Better jobs in cities are a pull factor, not a push factor.

mcqs.q: Mountainous high land like the Himalayas has:
options: The highest density in the world
mcqs.why: The correct answer is low density of population. Mountainous areas have few resources and difficult living conditions. Flat land like the Indus Valley in Sindh and Punjab has a high density.

mcqs.q: People are attracted towards urban centres mainly due to:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is economic opportunities. Better jobs, business and livelihood chances pull people from rural areas. Poverty and lack of jobs in villages push them to migrate.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a push factor in rural areas?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is poverty and unavailability of jobs. Droughts, water shortage and poor education and health also push people out. City jobs and services are pull factors instead.

mcqs.q: Shanty settlements in cities can be reduced by:
options: Proper city planning and low-cost housing
mcqs.why: The correct answer is proper city planning and low-cost housing. The chapter pairs each urban problem with such a solution. Traffic, for example, is controlled by better public transport and road planning.

mcqs.q: Pollution in urban cities can be reduced by:
options: Controlling factory smoke and vehicle emissions
mcqs.why: The correct answer is controlling factory smoke and vehicle emissions. More vehicles make cities hotter and more polluted. Enough clean water and waste management solve the cleanliness problem.

mcqs.q: Road networks impact humans by:
options: Connecting cities with villages so people travel easily for jobs, education, trade and medical help
Making villages empty in one day
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that roads connect places and ease travel for jobs, education, trade and medical help. They increase business and economic activity. Their negative side is more traffic, noise and air pollution.

mcqs.q: The major factors that influence the movement of people around the world include:
options: Only the weather of one season
Environmental, economic, social and political, and ecological factors
mcqs.why: The correct answer is these four groups of factors. Environmental factors include natural disasters, and social and political factors include discrimination, wars and conflicts. All these factors are connected with each other.

mcqs.q: Because of push factors, people migrate to cities such as:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is cities like Karachi, Lahore and Faisalabad. People come there from rural Punjab, KPK, Balochistan and the northern areas. This speeds up urbanization and makes urban populations grow rapidly.

lessons.title: Government and Democracy
lessons.notes_html:
Forms of Government — Who Holds Power

SystemWho holds powerRole of citizens
MonarchyOne hereditary ruler (king or queen); e.g. Saudi Arabia is an absolute monarchyOnly a few people advise the monarch; ordinary citizens have little say
DemocracyThe people, through voting; Pakistan is a representative democracyCitizens vote, run for office and enjoy basic individual rights
Authoritarianism / DictatorshipOne person or a small group (oligarchy: a collection of individuals rules over a nation)Limited political freedom; people cannot criticize the government

Key Terms

  • Democracy is "the government of the people, by the people, for the people" — a system where people form their government.
  • Political parties are a group of people with similar ideas and opinions; the party organization is the formal structure of the political party.
  • A manifesto is a party's public promises; it is an important benchmark for measuring the performance of a political party.
  • Left-wing politics refers to liberal political views.

How Citizens Can Improve Democracy in Pakistan

  • Vote honestly in every election and choose capable, honest candidates.
  • Stay informed, discuss public issues, pay taxes and obey the law.
  • Hold elected representatives accountable and respect the rights of others.
  • Useful changes: free, fair and regular elections; equal rule of law; an independent judiciary; accountability through a free press; more participation of women and minorities.

Activity

Collect information in two groups: one group on direct democracy (as in ancient Athens, where citizens made laws themselves) and the other on representative democracy (as in Pakistan, India and the United Kingdom, where elected representatives make laws). Discuss which type suits small communities and which suits large modern countries.

mcqs.q: Democracy is a system where:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a system where people form their government. It is famously defined as the government of the people, by the people, for the people. In a monarchy, by contrast, a king rules the state.

mcqs.q: A king rules the state in which political system?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is monarchy. In this system power is inherited by a king or queen. Saudi Arabia's political system is a monarchy, in fact an absolute monarchy.

mcqs.q: Saudi Arabia's political system is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is absolute monarchy. The book's exercise states this directly. Pakistan, in contrast, is a representative democracy.

mcqs.q: Pakistan is a:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a representative democracy. People elect representatives who make laws on their behalf. Direct democracy, as in ancient Athens, is practical only for small communities.

mcqs.q: Oligarchy is government in which:
options: All citizens vote on every law
A collection of individuals rules over a nation
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a small collection of individuals ruling over a nation. It is grouped with authoritarian systems in this chapter. In such systems people have limited political freedom.

mcqs.q: Political parties are a group of people with similar:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is ideas and opinions. The party organization is the formal structure of the political party. Parties organize the way a democratic country is governed.

mcqs.q: A manifesto is an important benchmark for measuring the performance of a:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a political party. A manifesto lists the party's promises to voters. After elections, people can judge the party against those promises.

mcqs.q: Left-wing politics refers to:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is liberal political views. The book's exercise states this directly. It is a term for one side of the political spectrum.

mcqs.q: In a democracy, citizens take part by:
options: Voting, running for office and enjoying basic individual rights
mcqs.why: The correct answer is full participation through voting, candidacy and rights. In a monarchy only a few advise the ruler. In authoritarian regimes people cannot criticize or oppose the government.

mcqs.q: Which change would improve democracy in Pakistan?
options: Holding completely free, fair and regular elections
mcqs.why: The correct answer is free, fair and regular elections. Other useful changes are equal rule of law, an independent judiciary and accountability through a free press. Wider participation of women and minorities also strengthens democracy.

lessons.title: Governing the World
lessons.notes_html:
International Law

International law is a set of rules derived from treaties, followed by states, which guides how countries deal with each other. It applies to all states in matters such as peace, trade, borders and human rights. International laws give all countries common rules for solving disputes, so disagreements are settled by talks and courts instead of by war.

The United Nations

  • The UNO was formed in 1945; fifty countries signed the UN Charter at San Francisco in June 1945, and the United Nations came into being on 24 October 1945, with headquarters in New York.
  • Its aim is to maintain peace and security in the world.
  • There are six organs of the UNO.

The Six Organs of the UN

OrganMain responsibility
General AssemblyAll member countries sit in it; discusses world peace and safety, approves the UN budget
Security CouncilMaintains peace, settles disputes; can impose sanctions and, as a last resort, allow the use of force
SecretariatUnder the Secretary-General, runs the UN's daily work
International Court of Justice (ICJ)The World Court; its fifteen judges (nine-year terms) settle legal disputes between countries and give legal advice
Economic and Social CouncilDeals with economic, social, cultural and humanitarian problems
Supervisory CouncilSupervises territories handed over to the UN

UN Agencies and the Kashmir Issue

  • UNICEF — United Nations International Children's Emergency Fund — looks after the health and welfare of children.
  • ILO stands for International Labour Organization.
  • The UN took up the Kashmir issue after partition; Security Council resolutions proposed that the people of Kashmir should decide their future through a free plebiscite under UN supervision.

Activity

Hold a mock session of the UN Security Council and discuss the Kashmir issue: members present the issue, hear both sides and speak for a peaceful solution through talks, ceasefire and respect for the wishes of the people concerned.

mcqs.q: A set of rules derived from treaties and followed by states is known as:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is international law. It guides how countries deal with each other in peace, trade, borders and human rights. Countries that sign a treaty are expected to honour it.

mcqs.q: There are ______ organs of the UNO.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is six organs. They are the General Assembly, Security Council, Secretariat, International Court of Justice, Economic and Social Council and Supervisory Council. Each has its own responsibilities.

mcqs.q: ICJ stands for:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is International Court of Justice. It is the World Court that settles legal disputes between countries. Its fifteen judges are chosen for nine years.

mcqs.q: The aim of the UNO is to maintain ______ in the world.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is peace and security. The UN was formed after the Second World War to save future generations from the horrors of war. It also protects basic human rights.

mcqs.q: The UNO was formed in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1945. Fifty countries signed the UN Charter at San Francisco in June 1945. The United Nations came into being on 24 October 1945, with headquarters in New York.

mcqs.q: UNICEF stands for:
options: United Nations International Children's Emergency Fund
United Nations Internal Children's Education Fund
mcqs.why: The correct answer is United Nations International Children's Emergency Fund. UNICEF looks after the health and general welfare of children. It provides medicines, food support and help for education and nutrition.

mcqs.q: ILO stands for:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is International Labour Organization. It is one of the agencies of the UN system. UNICEF, in contrast, works for children.

mcqs.q: The main function of the Security Council is to:
options: Run the daily work of the UN
Maintain peace in the world and prevent war between nations
mcqs.why: The correct answer is maintaining peace and preventing war. It arranges dialogue between disputing nations and can impose sanctions. Approving the budget is the work of the General Assembly.

mcqs.q: The International Court of Justice has how many judges?
options: Five judges, chosen for five years
Fifty judges, one from each country
Fifteen judges, chosen for nine years
mcqs.why: The correct answer is fifteen judges with nine-year terms. They are chosen by the General Assembly and the Security Council. The Court also gives legal advice to UN organs and agencies.

mcqs.q: On the Kashmir issue, UN Security Council resolutions proposed:
options: A free plebiscite under UN supervision so Kashmiris decide their future
Immediate division by a military line only
Handing Kashmir to a third country
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a free plebiscite under UN supervision. The UN also keeps military observers in the region to watch the ceasefire. It continues to urge Pakistan and India to solve the issue peacefully through dialogue.

lessons.title: Human Rights and Role as Global Citizens
lessons.notes_html:
What Are Human Rights?

Human rights are the basic rights and freedoms that belong to every person in the world, from birth until death. They are based on shared values like dignity, fairness, equality and respect, and they are defined and protected by law. Every person has these rights regardless of caste, culture, race or creed, and nobody can take them away. Fundamental rights are guaranteed under the Constitution of the country.

History of Human Rights

YearDevelopment
539 BCKing Cyrus conquered Babylon and declared that all people could choose their own religion, establishing racial equality
1215Magna Carta in Britain
1679Habeas Corpus Act in Britain
1689Bill of Rights in Britain
1948United Nations adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR)

Legal and Moral Responsibilities

  • A legal responsibility is a duty required by the laws of the country and enforced by the government; not performing it can be punished.
  • A moral responsibility is something a person should do because their own sense of what is good and fair tells them it is right.
  • A responsible citizen abides by the law of the land, pays taxes timely and respects the rights of others.

Responsibilities of a Global Citizen

  • Ensure everyone is aware of their rights and help others achieve and enjoy their human rights.
  • Speak out for things that matter and support groups that protect human rights.
  • Listen to the stories of others and take a stand against discrimination.
  • Choose goods that are made fairly and ethically.
  • The features of human rights: universal (applicable to all humans everywhere), inalienable (cannot be removed), indivisible (cannot be divided) and interrelated (all rights depend on each other).

mcqs.q: Magna Carta was presented in the year:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1215. The Magna Carta was an early British step in the history of human rights. The Bill of Rights came much later, in 1689.

mcqs.q: The Bill of Rights was passed in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1689. It followed the Habeas Corpus Act of 1679 in Britain. The UDHR was adopted far later, in 1948.

mcqs.q: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1948. The United Nations adopted it after the Second World War. It lists, for the first time, the basic rights and freedoms of all people.

mcqs.q: Fundamental rights are guaranteed under the ______ of the country.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Constitution. Fundamental rights are defined and protected by law. A manifesto is only a political party's list of promises.

mcqs.q: UDHR stands for:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Universal Declaration of Human Rights. It was prepared by more than fifty countries and adopted by the UN in 1948. It declares the rights of every person in the world.

mcqs.q: Human rights belong to every person:
options: Only after the age of eighteen
From birth until death, regardless of caste, culture, race or creed
Only to citizens who pay taxes
mcqs.why: The correct answer is from birth until death, for everyone without distinction. They are based on dignity, fairness, equality and respect. Nobody can take them away.

mcqs.q: A legal responsibility differs from a moral responsibility because:
options: It comes only from personal feelings
It is required by the laws of the country and enforced by the government
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that legal duties are required by law and enforced by the government. A moral duty comes from one's own values and conscience. Not performing a legal duty can be punished by the state.

mcqs.q: A responsible citizen is one who abides by the law, pays taxes timely and:
options: Works only for his own family
mcqs.why: The correct answer is respects the rights of others. The book completes the definition in this way. Such a citizen also helps others enjoy their human rights.

mcqs.q: The foundation of human rights was laid when King Cyrus conquered Babylon in 539 BC and declared:
options: That all people had the right to choose their own religion
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the right of all people to choose their own religion. He also established racial equality. Later milestones were the Magna Carta (1215) and the UDHR (1948).

mcqs.q: Human rights are called 'inalienable' because:
options: They apply only in one country
They can be sold to others
A human is born with them and no one can remove, bar or undo them in any circumstances
They can be divided into parts
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that they cannot be removed from a person in any circumstances. 'Universal' means they apply to all humans everywhere, while 'indivisible' means they cannot be divided partially.

lessons.title: Children's Rights
lessons.notes_html:
The Child and the Convention

  • The child is a growing future adult, who has no means to protect themselves.
  • Children's rights were recognised with the adoption of the Declaration of Geneva in 1924.
  • A convention can be understood as an agreement among countries to act in a particular manner.
  • The Convention on the Rights of the Child (CRC) gives governments a framework for laws and policies on children.

The 3Ps of Children's Rights

CategoryWhat it covers
ProtectionSafety from abuse, neglect, exploitation and harmful work
ProvisionEducation, health care and basic economic welfare
ParticipationFreedom of thought, conscience and religion, and a voice in matters affecting the child

Why Children's Rights Are Still Not Protected

Although the CRC and the UDHR give children clear rights, they are still not protected in many places because of poverty, ignorance and weak enforcement of laws. Many families are forced by poverty to send their children to work instead of school, and many people do not even know that children have special rights.

Education and Child Labour

  • Education takes children out of workshops and factories and places them in schools, where they are safe.
  • Educated children learn skills for better jobs as adults, so they are not trapped in low-paid labour for life.
  • If all grown-ups reached at least secondary school, poverty could be cut by more than half.
  • Citizens can protect child rights by not employing children, sending their own children to school and reporting abuse or labour, for example to the Sindh Child Protection Authority, established in 2011.
  • Iqbal Masih, sold as a bonded labourer to a carpet factory, escaped at the age of eleven and spoke for working children everywhere.

mcqs.q: Children's rights were recognised with the adoption of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Declaration of Geneva of 1924. It was the first recognition of children's special rights. The UDHR of 1948 covers the rights of all human beings.

mcqs.q: The child rights in the Convention fall into three categories: protection, ______ and ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is provision and participation. Together with protection, these are called the 3Ps. Provision covers education and health care, while participation gives the child a voice.

mcqs.q: A convention can be understood as:
options: A meeting of one political party
