An agreement among countries to act in a particular manner
A court judgement in one country
mcqs.why: The correct answer is an agreement among countries. The CRC is such a convention for children's rights. Governments use it as a framework for their laws and policies.

mcqs.q: The 'Protection' category of child rights covers:
options: Safety from abuse, exploitation and harmful work
mcqs.why: The correct answer is safety from abuse, exploitation and harmful work. Provision covers education, health care and welfare. Participation covers freedom of thought and a voice in matters affecting the child.

mcqs.q: Children's rights are still not protected in many places mainly because of:
options: Poverty, ignorance and weak enforcement of laws
mcqs.why: The correct answer is poverty, ignorance and weak enforcement. Poor families are forced to send children to work instead of school. Many people do not even know that children have special rights.

mcqs.q: Education can end child labour because it:
options: Takes children out of workshops and factories and places them in schools
Makes factory work easier for children
Allows children to work at night
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that education places children in schools where they are safe. Educated children later get better jobs and escape low-paid labour. If all adults reached secondary school, poverty could be cut by more than half.

mcqs.q: The Sindh Child Protection Authority was established in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 2011. It was established to eliminate child abuse and violence against children. Citizens can report child labour and abuse to such bodies.

mcqs.q: Iqbal Masih is remembered because he:
options: Escaped bonded labour in a carpet factory at the age of eleven and spoke for working children
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that he escaped bonded labour and spoke for working children everywhere. His story shows how serious child labour is. He had been sold to a carpet factory as a child.

mcqs.q: The guiding principles of the CRC include:
options: Non-discrimination and the best interest of the child
mcqs.why: The correct answer is non-discrimination and the best interest of the child. Survival and development, and participation, are the other guiding principles. They guide every policy concerning children.

mcqs.q: Citizens can play their role in protecting child rights by:
options: Not employing children and sending their own children to school
mcqs.why: The correct answer is not employing children and spreading awareness about their rights. Citizens should also report child abuse or labour to the authorities. This supports the work of bodies like the Sindh Child Protection Authority.

lessons.title: Role of Political Parties
lessons.notes_html:
Party Abbreviations

AbbreviationFull name
PPPPakistan Peoples Party
PTIPakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf
ANPAwami National Party
PML-NPakistan Muslim League-Nawaz
JIJamaat-e-Islami

Key Terms

  • A political party is a group of people who share similar ideas about how a country should be run and work together to win elections and run the government.
  • A manifesto is a public statement in which a party tells everyone what it wants to do if it wins the election — a well-defined list of promises circulated among voters.
  • Elections are the process through which citizens choose their representatives by voting; free and fair elections are the foundation of democracy.
  • Parliament is the elected law-making body of a country; in Pakistan it consists of the National Assembly and the Senate. It makes laws, approves the budget and checks the work of the government.
  • A democratic government is a government of the people, by the people and for the people, working on rule of law, human rights, political equality and accountability.

Activity

Make a list of the political parties participating in local, provincial and national assemblies in your area, and write the names of their local leaders in your constituency. Students should find the names from their own area after enquiry, because they differ from constituency to constituency.

mcqs.q: PPP stands for:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Pakistan Peoples Party. The chapter's exercise gives the full forms of the main parties. PTI, similarly, stands for Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf.

mcqs.q: PTI stands for:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf. It is one of the main political parties of Pakistan. ANP stands for Awami National Party.

mcqs.q: ANP stands for:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Awami National Party. The exercise lists it among the main parties. JI stands for Jamaat-e-Islami.

mcqs.q: PML-N stands for:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz. It is one of the major parties contesting elections in Pakistan. PPP stands for Pakistan Peoples Party.

mcqs.q: JI stands for:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Jamaat-e-Islami. These abbreviations are part of the chapter's basic knowledge about parties. Knowing them helps citizens follow politics and elections.

mcqs.q: A political party is:
options: A group of people who share similar ideas about how a country should be run
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a group sharing similar ideas about running the country. Its members contest elections and form or oppose the government. Political parties are essential for a modern democracy.

mcqs.q: A manifesto is:
options: A public statement of what a party wants to do if it wins the election
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a public statement of the party's promises. It is circulated among voters to attract their support. It also helps people judge the party's performance later.

mcqs.q: Elections are:
options: The process through which citizens choose their representatives by voting
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the voting process by which citizens choose representatives. The winning party or candidate forms the government for a fixed period. Free and fair elections are the foundation of democracy.

mcqs.q: Parliament in Pakistan consists of:
options: The National Assembly and the Senate
The Supreme Court and High Courts
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the National Assembly and the Senate. Parliament makes and passes laws and approves the budget. It also keeps a check on the work of the government.

mcqs.q: A democratic government works on principles such as:
options: Rule of law, respect for human rights, political equality and accountability
mcqs.why: The correct answer is rule of law, human rights, political equality and accountability. Such a government is of the people, by the people and for the people. People can change it peacefully through elections.

lessons.title: Markets and Prices
lessons.notes_html:
Demand, Supply and Price

  • An increase in the price of a product reduces the amount purchased, because consumers substitute other products for the one whose price has risen (the law of demand).
  • A change in the price of a product itself does not change its demand; it causes a movement along the same demand curve — only the quantity demanded changes.
  • Demand itself changes when other factors change, such as the price of a close substitute, consumer incomes or consumer tastes.
  • A shortage occurs where the market price leads to quantity demanded being greater than quantity supplied.
  • A surplus means more goods are supplied than demanded at the current price; prices tend to fall, consumers gain, but producers earn less and unsold stock is wasted.
  • Equilibrium is the point where quantity demanded equals quantity supplied.

Worked Example — Eggs at a Funfair

PriceQuantity demandedQuantity supplied
$2.108007,200
$1.801,6004,800
$1.602,4002,400
$1.403,200800
$1.204,100200

The equilibrium price is $1.60, because at this price the quantity demanded (2,400 eggs) exactly equals the quantity supplied (2,400 eggs). If the price is set at $1.80, only 1,600 eggs will be sold and the rest will remain unsold as a surplus.

How Prices Are Controlled in a Market

In a market economy, prices, demand and supply control each other. If demand rises or supply falls, the price rises, which discourages buyers and encourages producers to supply more. If there is a surplus, the price falls, which increases demand and reduces supply until the market reaches equilibrium.

Reading a Demand Curve

On the demand curve in the book (price $40 at zero quantity, falling to $0 at 20 units): at a price of $30, 5 units are demanded; at $20, 10 units are demanded, and the consumer surplus at $20 equals $100.

mcqs.q: An increase in the price of a product will reduce the amount purchased because:
options: Consumers will substitute other products for the one whose price has risen
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that consumers substitute other products. This is the law of demand at work. The higher price does not raise real incomes; it reduces what people can buy.

mcqs.q: Which of the following will NOT cause the demand for product K to change?
options: A change in the price of K
A change in the price of close-substitute product J
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a change in the price of K itself. It only changes the quantity demanded, shown as a movement along the curve. Substitutes, incomes and tastes shift demand itself.

mcqs.q: When supply falls, what happens to quantity demanded in equilibrium?
options: Supply has no effect on it
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that quantity demanded decreases. With less supply the price rises, and buyers purchase less. The market moves to a new equilibrium.

mcqs.q: A shortage in a market occurs where:
options: There are fewer producers than consumers
Quantity demanded is greater than quantity supplied at the market price
mcqs.why: The correct answer is where quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied. Shortages can be controlled by increasing production and supply and removing barriers to imports. Hoarding makes shortages worse.

mcqs.q: In the eggs example, the equilibrium price is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is $1.60. At this price, quantity demanded (2,400) exactly equals quantity supplied (2,400). There is neither a shortage nor a surplus.

mcqs.q: If the funfair organizers set the price of eggs at $1.80, how many eggs will be sold?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1,600 eggs. At $1.80 buyers want only 1,600 eggs although sellers offer 4,800. The rest remain unsold as a surplus.

mcqs.q: A positive effect of a surplus of goods is that:
options: Prices tend to fall, so consumers can buy goods more cheaply
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that prices fall and consumers gain. The negative effects fall on producers: less profit, wasted stock and cuts in production and jobs. A surplus means supply is greater than demand.

mcqs.q: If the price of a chocolate bar increases, what changes?
options: Its quantity demanded decreases — a movement along the demand curve
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a movement along the same demand curve. The curve itself does not shift when the good's own price changes. Demand changes only when income, tastes or substitute prices change.

mcqs.q: On the book's demand curve, if the price of the good is $20, the quantity demanded is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 10 units. At the higher price of $30, only 5 units are demanded. At $20 the consumer surplus equals $100.

mcqs.q: Shortages of goods in the market can be controlled by:
options: Increasing production and supply and removing barriers to imports
mcqs.why: The correct answer is increasing supply and removing import barriers. The price may also be allowed to rise a little so demand falls and supply increases. Balance is restored at equilibrium.

lessons.title: International Trade
lessons.notes_html:
Key Terms

TermMeaning
Barter systemTrade done by direct exchange of goods and services
WholesalerIn the modern era, goods and services are first delivered to the wholesaler in huge quantity
Export tradeSelling goods and services from the domestic country to other countries
Import tradeBringing goods and services from other countries to the home country
Entrepot tradeImporting goods from one country and exporting them to another after adding some value
Balance of tradeThe difference between the value of exports and imports of a country in a given time frame

Domestic and International Trade

Domestic trade takes place within the borders of one country, using its own currency and rules, while international trade takes place between different countries, using foreign exchange and international rules. Five benefits of international trade: specialization through comparative advantage; economies of scale lowering cost per item; competition improving price and quality; transfer of technology; and more jobs.

Pakistan's Trade Deficit

  • Pakistan's imports grow much faster than its exports: it imports petroleum products, machinery, iron and steel and edible oil.
  • Its exports are limited to a few items like cotton products and rice.
  • Exports can be increased by improving quality, adding value, finding new markets and supporting sports goods, surgical instruments and IT; imports can be decreased by producing more goods locally and saving energy.

Regional Trade Agreements

Regional Trade Agreements (RTAs) reduce trade barriers between member countries. Examples: the China-Pakistan Free Trade Agreement (CPFTA), NAFTA, ASEAN, the Trans Pacific Partnership (TPP) and RCEP. In South Asia, SAARC formed SAPTA in 1993 and SAFTA in 2006, while the European Union has the highest regional trade integration in the world.

Activity — Gains from Trade

A wholesaler buys note books at Rs. 18 and pencils at Rs. 3 from a manufacturer and sells them at Rs. 25 and Rs. 5. The wholesaler gains Rs. 7 on each note book and Rs. 2 on each pencil, while the manufacturer also gains by selling in bulk above its earlier prices — trade benefits both sides.

mcqs.q: In the ancient barter system, trade was done by:
options: Direct exchange of goods and services
mcqs.why: The correct answer is direct exchange of goods and services. Barter needed no money at all. In the modern era, goods first reach the wholesaler in huge quantity.

mcqs.q: Selling goods and services from the domestic country to other countries is known as:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is export trade. Bringing goods from other countries into the home country is import trade. The two together make international trade.

mcqs.q: Bringing goods and services from other countries to the home country is called:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is import trade. Pakistan imports items such as petroleum products, machinery and edible oil. Selling domestic goods abroad is export trade.

mcqs.q: Entrepot trade means:
options: Importing goods from one country and exporting them to another after adding some value
mcqs.why: The correct answer is re-exporting imported goods after adding value. It is a third type of foreign trade besides export and import. The value addition is what makes it different from simple transit.

mcqs.q: The balance of trade is:
options: The total population of a country
The difference between the value of exports and imports of a country in a given time frame
The price of goods in a market
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the difference between exports and imports. When imports exceed exports, the country has a trade deficit. Pakistan's deficit is increasing because imports grow faster than exports.

mcqs.q: In the modern and global era, goods and services are first delivered in huge quantity to the:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the wholesaler. Goods are delivered to the wholesaler in huge quantity before reaching retailers and customers. In the class activity, the wholesaler earned profit on both note books and pencils.

mcqs.q: One benefit of international trade is:
options: Technology is transferred from developed to developing countries
mcqs.why: The correct answer is technology transfer. Other benefits are comparative advantage, economies of scale, better price and quality through competition, and more jobs. Trade therefore raises living standards.

mcqs.q: Pakistan's trade deficit is increasing mainly because:
options: Its imports are growing much faster than its exports
mcqs.why: The correct answer is imports growing faster than exports. Pakistan imports petroleum, machinery, iron and steel and edible oil. Its exports are limited to a few items like cotton products and rice.

mcqs.q: Pakistan can increase its exports by:
options: Improving quality, adding value and finding new markets
mcqs.why: The correct answer is improving quality, value addition and new markets. Supporting sports goods, surgical instruments and IT also helps. Imports can be decreased by producing more goods locally and saving energy.

mcqs.q: SAARC formed SAFTA in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 2006. SAARC had earlier formed SAPTA in 1993. The European Union has the highest regional trade integration in the world.

lessons.title: Entrepreneurship
lessons.notes_html:
Key Terms

  • The word entrepreneur originates from the French language.
  • Entrepreneurship is a course of purposeful action based on informed decisions.
  • Some entrepreneurs start their own businesses because they like to build organizations.
  • The jobs created by entrepreneurship lead to equitable distribution of income.
  • Deal makers are the type of entrepreneur who dislike to manage and commit themselves to an organization over the long run.

Types of Entrepreneurs

TypeWhat they love doing
Technical entrepreneursInventing things and creating new markets with advanced technology
Organization buildersBuilding and growing companies by developing people, systems and structures
Deal makersMaking initial business deals to start new ventures, but not managing them for long

Why Risk Taking Is Important

Every new business involves danger and uncertainty, and no profit or growth is possible without taking some risk. An entrepreneur makes informed decisions knowing that both good and bad outcomes are possible. Careful risk taking allows the entrepreneur to use new opportunities before others.

Qualities and Sacrifices

  • Qualities of a successful entrepreneur: willpower, management, passion, common sense (smarts), self-assurance, devotion, inspiration and flexibility.
  • An entrepreneur sacrifices a steady income, fixed working hours and job security, and may face periods with no income at all; he should save at least six months of expenses before fully committing to the business.
  • Role in society: entrepreneurs create new markets and innovation, create jobs, reduce unemployment and improve living standards.

Activity

For each situation in the Risk vs. Opportunity exercise, write the risk involved and one possible opportunity, and explain how you would minimize the risk — for example, before using your entire savings of Rs. 1,000 in a new business, make a careful plan, start on a small scale and keep a part of the savings aside.

mcqs.q: The word 'entrepreneur' originates from which language?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is French. The chapter's exercise states this directly. Entrepreneurship itself is defined as a course of purposeful action based on informed decisions.

mcqs.q: Entrepreneurship is:
options: A course of purposeful action based on informed decisions
mcqs.why: The correct answer is purposeful action based on informed decisions. An entrepreneur knows both good and bad outcomes are possible. Careful decisions separate entrepreneurship from blind gambling.

mcqs.q: Some entrepreneurs start their own businesses because they like to build:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is organizations. Such entrepreneurs are called organization builders. They enjoy developing people, systems and structures.

mcqs.q: The jobs created by entrepreneurship lead to equitable distribution of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is income. Entrepreneurs create jobs and reduce unemployment. Their taxes also expand government resources for services and infrastructure.

mcqs.q: Which type of entrepreneur dislikes managing an organization over the long run?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is deal makers. They thrive on making initial business deals to start ventures. Organization builders, in contrast, enjoy growing companies over time.

mcqs.q: Technical entrepreneurs love:
options: Inventing things and creating new markets with advanced technology
mcqs.why: The correct answer is inventing things and creating new markets with technology. This is the first of the three types described in the chapter. Deal makers and organization builders are the other two.

mcqs.q: Risk taking is important to entrepreneurs because:
options: No profit or growth is possible without taking some risk
Risk removes the need for planning
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that profit and growth require some risk. Every new business involves danger and uncertainty. Informed, careful risk taking lets the entrepreneur use opportunities before others.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a quality that makes an entrepreneur successful?
options: Giving up after the first failure
mcqs.why: The correct answer is willpower, passion and flexibility, along with management, common sense, self-assurance, devotion and inspiration. Willpower and devotion keep him working after failures. Flexibility helps him adapt to changing market needs.

mcqs.q: Before fully committing to a business, an entrepreneur should save at least:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is six months of expenses. An entrepreneur sacrifices a steady income, fixed hours and job security. This saving protects him during periods with no income.

mcqs.q: Entrepreneurs help society by:
options: Creating jobs, reducing unemployment and improving living standards
mcqs.why: The correct answer is creating jobs and improving living standards. They also create new markets and drive innovation and technological advancement. This leads to economic growth for the whole society.

lessons.title: Cultural Heritage Conserving Skills
lessons.notes_html:
What Is Cultural Heritage?

Cultural heritage is the cultural treasure we inherit from the past, live with in the present, and hand down to the future. It includes monuments, historical places and archaeological sites which hold value in history, science and art. UNESCO defines it as the physical objects and intangible qualities passed down through generations. UNESCO is the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization; it came into being on 4 November 1946 and its headquarters is in Paris, France.

Six World Cultural Heritage Sites in Pakistan

SiteProvinceDistrict
Moen Jo DaroSindhLarkana
Takht-i-Bhai and Bahr-i-BahlolKhyber PakhtunkhwaMardan
TaxilaPunjabRawalpindi
Lahore Fort (Shahi Qila) and Shalimar GardenPunjabLahore
Monuments of MakliSindhThatta
Rohtas Fort (Rohtas Qila)PunjabJhelum

Moveable and Immoveable Assets

  • Moveable cultural heritage assets can be moved from one place to another — paintings, coins, utensils, sculptures and manuscripts — and are conserved in museums.
  • Immoveable assets cannot be moved — archaeological sites, architectural sites and monuments — and are conserved in their original shape and setting.
  • Every nation conserves its heritage because conservation passes these assets to the next generations; without care, deterioration slowly destroys them.

Heritage and Tourism

Tourists visit a country to see its museums, monuments and heritage sites, and this generates opportunities of trade and employment, so cultural tourism becomes a source of economic growth. The Constitution of Pakistan also protects culture: Article 28 gives citizens the right to preserve and promote their distinct language, script and culture, and Article 33 requires the State to discourage parochial and other prejudices.

mcqs.q: Moen Jo Daro is located in which district and province?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Larkana district of Sindh. Moen Jo Daro is one of the six World Cultural Heritage sites in Pakistan. The Monuments of Makli are in Thatta district.

mcqs.q: Takht-i-Bhai and Bahr-i-Bahlol are located in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Mardan district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Taxila is in Rawalpindi district of Punjab. Both are among Pakistan's six World Heritage sites.

mcqs.q: Taxila is located in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Rawalpindi district of Punjab. Lahore Fort and Shalimar Garden are in Lahore district. Taxila is a famous archaeological site of the Gandhara civilization.

mcqs.q: The Monuments of Makli are located in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Thatta district of Sindh. Rohtas Fort is in Jhelum district of Punjab. Makli is one of the largest necropolises and a World Heritage site.

mcqs.q: Rohtas Fort is located in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Jhelum district of Punjab. It completes the list of six World Cultural Heritage sites in Pakistan given in the chapter. Lahore Fort is in Lahore district.

mcqs.q: The full form of UNESCO is:
options: United Nations Economic and Social Council Organization
Universal Network for Education and Culture
United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization
mcqs.why: The correct answer is United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization. It came into being on 4 November 1946. Its headquarters is in Paris, France.

mcqs.q: UNESCO's headquarters is in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Paris, France. UNESCO works for peace, education, science, culture and the protection of world heritage. The UN headquarters, in contrast, is in New York.

mcqs.q: Moveable cultural heritage assets are:
options: Objects that can be moved, such as paintings, coins, utensils, sculptures and manuscripts
mcqs.why: The correct answer is objects that can be moved from one place to another. They are conserved in museums, where they can be protected properly. Looting and stealing of such assets is a serious threat in Pakistan.

mcqs.q: Immoveable cultural heritage assets are conserved by:
options: Keeping them in their original shape and manner, in their own original setting
mcqs.why: The correct answer is keeping them in their original setting and shape. Repairs for climatic damage must not alter their originality at all. Sites and monuments cannot be moved like paintings or coins.

mcqs.q: Nations conserve cultural heritage because:
options: Heritage has no value for the future
Conservation passes these assets on to the next generations
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to pass the assets to future generations. Heritage transmits experiences, skills and knowledge between generations. Without care, deterioration slowly destroys these assets completely.

lessons.title: The Social Institutions and the Change in Society
lessons.notes_html:
Social Institutions and Change

  • The family is the basic institution of society.
  • Change happens everywhere, but the rate of change varies from place to place.
  • The five social institutions are family, political, educational, economic and religious institutions.
  • The invention of mobile phones is a technological advancement.
  • An increase in the number of births, deaths or migration causes population change; demographic change is caused by an increase in birth and a decline in death and migration of populations.

Technological Advancements That Changed People's Ways

Four technological advancements are the mobile phone, the television, electricity and motor vehicles such as buses, rickshaws and motorcycles. The mobile phone changed the way we communicate and write, as people now send text messages instead of letters and postcards.

Family Structures

StructureFeatures
PatriarchalMale members hold the main authority
MatriarchalFemale members hold the main authority
Inclusive familyMale and female members share economic and household responsibilities and help each other in chores

Activity

Interview the eldest person in your family or neighbourhood about the changes in society caused by the arrival of a technology such as electricity in your locality, and note the positive changes it brought, such as fans, lights, television, water pumps, better study time for children and improved business and communication.

mcqs.q: The ______ is the basic institution of society.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the family. It is the first institution every child belongs to. The other social institutions are political, educational, economic and religious.

mcqs.q: Change happens everywhere, but:
options: The rate of change varies from place to place
It happens at the same speed everywhere
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that the rate of change varies from place to place. Some societies change quickly and others slowly. This is a basic point of the chapter.

mcqs.q: The invention of mobile phones is a ______ advancement.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a technological advancement. Mobile phones changed how we communicate and write, as text messages replaced letters and postcards. Television, electricity and motor vehicles are other examples.

mcqs.q: An increase in the number of births, deaths or migration causes ______ change.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is population change. These three factors decide how the population of a place grows or falls. Demographic change is linked to rising births and declining deaths.

mcqs.q: Demographic change is caused by:
options: An increase in birth and a decline in death and migration of populations
mcqs.why: The correct answer is rising births with declining deaths and migration. Together these change the size and structure of the population. Mobile phones are a technological, not demographic, change.

mcqs.q: In an inclusive family:
options: Male and female members share economic and household responsibilities
Only the father takes all decisions
Children are not given any duties
mcqs.why: The correct answer is shared responsibilities between male and female members. Both work and both help in household chores such as cooking and cleaning. No single person carries the whole burden, and decisions are shared.

mcqs.q: Which of these is one of the five social institutions?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the religious institution. The five are family, political, educational, economic and religious institutions. Each has its own strengths and weaknesses in society.

mcqs.q: A strength of the family as an institution is that it:
options: Gives love, care and basic training to a child
Provides all laws of the country
mcqs.why: The correct answer is love, care and basic training. The chapter's group activity uses exactly this example. A weakness is that a family can also be too strict and stop a member from choosing a new path.

mcqs.q: When electricity arrived in a locality, a positive change was that:
options: Children could study at night and water pumps and machines made life easy
mcqs.why: The correct answer is easier life with study at night, pumps and machines. The elder's interview in the chapter describes life before electricity as limited to daylight hours. Work, education and communication all improved afterwards.

mcqs.q: A local conflict over a boundary wall and drainage in the chapter ended when:
options: The elders and the local council sat with both families and settled it according to the record
The police closed the street forever
mcqs.why: The correct answer is settlement by elders and the local council. They listened to both sides and settled the boundary and drainage according to the record. Both families accepted the decision and peace returned.

lessons.title: Development of Cultures in the Societies of the World
lessons.notes_html:
Material and Non-Material Culture

  • Culture is not only represented through physical objects; a major part of culture lies in the way people behave.
  • Dresses and architecture are part of material culture. Three material components of culture are dresses, architecture and food.
  • In Pakistan, people of Sindh wear Sindhi Topi and Ajrak, in Baluchistan men wear a white turban, and in Punjab people wear colourful turbans and dhoti.
  • Famous foods include Biryani, Pulao, Nihari, Sajji and Tikka; the 'Palla' fish is the traditional food of Sindh province.
  • Modern information technology and social media have played a vital role in promoting culture and tourism.
  • Ayesha Malik has been selected as the first female judge of the Supreme Court of Pakistan.

Rituals and Identity

Rituals are religious or social ceremonies performed in a prescribed manner. In the culture of Sindh, during a wedding the bride and bridegroom are seated on a cotton quilt covered with a red sheet and their heads are bumped to each other; this ritual is called Laon. Such rituals connect us with our region, family and traditions and show others who we are.

Continuity from the Indus Valley

Three objects found in the Indus Valley civilization that can be seen in our society today are pottery and utensils, jewellery and ornaments, and tools and wheeled carts. Similar pots, jewellery and the wheel are still used in our homes and markets, which shows the continuity of that ancient culture.

Development of Cultures — Timeline

PeriodFeatures
Indus Valley CivilizationMohen-Jo-Daro, Mehrgarh and Harappa — urban planning and crafts
Gandhara CivilizationTaxila and Takht-i-Bhai — Buddhist art and learning
Islamic CultureKalhora (Abbasi) period — tombs and masjids in Sindh
Mughal EraLahore Fort and Shalimar Garden — art and architecture
Modern AgeTelevision, radio, satellite channels and social media promote cultures worldwide

Gender Roles and Diversity

The actions considered appropriate to a person's gender, as defined by cultural practices, are called gender roles, but they are not definite and rigid; women are now participating in every walk of life. Cultural diversity in Pakistan supports creativity, innovation, cultural tourism and the economy.

mcqs.q: A major part of culture lies in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the way people behave. Culture is not only represented through physical objects. Behaviour, rituals and customs form its major part.

mcqs.q: Dresses and architecture are part of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is material culture. Material culture includes all physical things a group uses, like tools, clothes, buildings and food. Behaviour belongs to the non-material side.

mcqs.q: Who has been selected as the first female judge of the Supreme Court of Pakistan?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Ayesha Malik. The chapter gives her selection as an example of changing gender roles. Women are now participating in every walk of life.

mcqs.q: The 'Palla' fish is the traditional food of which province?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Sindh. Food is a material component of culture, and each region has its special dishes. Biryani, Pulao, Nihari, Sajji and Tikka are famous all over the world.

mcqs.q: Modern ______ and ______ have played a vital role in promoting culture and tourism.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is information technology and social media. The chapter's timeline also notes television, radio and satellite channels promoting cultures worldwide. These tools spread cultural images quickly across the globe.

mcqs.q: Three material components of culture are:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is dresses, architecture and food. These are physical things a group of people uses. Beliefs and customs are non-material parts of culture.

mcqs.q: In the culture of Sindh, the wedding ritual in which the heads of the bride and bridegroom are bumped to each other is called:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Laon. The bride and bridegroom are seated on a cotton quilt covered with a red sheet for this ritual. Such rituals connect us with our region, family and traditions.

mcqs.q: Which objects from the Indus Valley civilization can still be seen in our society today?
options: Pottery and utensils, jewellery and ornaments, and tools and wheeled carts
mcqs.why: The correct answer is pottery, jewellery and tools and wheeled carts. The people of Mohen-Jo-Daro and Harappa used them in daily life. Their continued use shows the continuity of that ancient culture.

mcqs.q: Gender roles are:
options: Actions considered appropriate to a gender by cultural practices, and they are not definite and rigid
mcqs.why: The correct answer is culturally defined and changeable. Families even choose toys and colours according to the sex of a newborn. With time, women now fly planes and hold high ranks in the military and police.

mcqs.q: Cultural diversity in Pakistan is advantageous because it:
options: Stops people from learning from each other
Supports creativity, innovation, cultural tourism and the economy
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that diversity supports creativity, tourism and the economy. Communities earn by presenting their artifacts and handicrafts in the market. People also learn from each other by sharing ideas and traditions.

lessons.title: Conflict Resolution
lessons.notes_html:
What Conflict Is Based On

  • Conflict is based on differences.
  • Conflict and its constructive management is integral to democratic citizenship.
  • If both parties attempt to win and make the other lose, this situation is called win-lose (competing).
  • Asoka, the Mauryan ruler, abolished and ended slavery.
  • A judge is a fine example of an arbitrator.

Three Ways to Manage a Conflict

  • Communication — both parties listen to each other and explain their positions and interests without blaming each other.
  • Negotiation — the parties work together to find a solution that meets the interests of all.
  • Compromising — both parties give up something and get something, so the problem is settled peacefully without violence.

How Communication Prevents Conflict

Most conflicts grow when people do not listen to each other and misunderstand the other person's position and interests. Talking calmly and listening can solve a small disagreement, such as over a seat or a turn in a game, before it turns into a fight. Communication is a constructive response to conflict, while violence is a highly destructive response.

Steps of Effective Negotiation

StepAction
1Identify position and interests
2Present and listen
3Brainstorm possible solutions
4Strike off solutions that are unacceptable
5Choose an acceptable solution
6Make an action plan

Activity

Work in groups: take an international conflict, such as the Jammu and Kashmir conflict going on since 1947, and devise ways to end it. A negotiated and peaceful settlement is better than war, because war only destroys lives and property, while negotiation and mediation can give a lasting solution acceptable to all parties.

mcqs.q: Conflict is based on:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is differences. Where people differ in interests or views, conflict can arise. Its constructive management is integral to democratic citizenship.

mcqs.q: Conflict and its constructive management is integral to ______ citizenship.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is democratic citizenship. Citizens of a democracy learn to handle differences peacefully. Violence is a destructive response, not a democratic one.

mcqs.q: If both parties attempt to win and make the other lose, the situation is called:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is win-lose, also called competing. In compromising, by contrast, both parties give up something and get something. Negotiation aims at a solution meeting the interests of all.

mcqs.q: Asoka, the Mauryan ruler, abolished and ended:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is slavery. The chapter gives Asoka as a historical example of a peaceful and just ruler. His example shows rulers can end cruel practices.

mcqs.q: A judge is a fine example of an:
options: Mediator chosen by one side only
mcqs.why: The correct answer is an arbitrator. An arbitrator listens to both parties and gives a decision. Like a judge, he is neutral between the parties.

mcqs.q: Three ways to manage a conflict are:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is communication, negotiation and compromising. In communication, parties listen without blaming each other. In compromising, both sides give up something and get something.

mcqs.q: Communication can prevent a conflict because:
options: Most conflicts grow when people do not listen to each other and misunderstand the other's position
It replaces the need for any solution
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that listening removes misunderstanding. Calm talk can solve a disagreement over a seat or a turn in a game before it becomes a fight. Communication is constructive, while violence is destructive.

mcqs.q: The first step of effective negotiation is to:
options: Identify each side's position and interests
mcqs.why: The correct answer is identifying position and interests. Only then do the parties present, listen and brainstorm solutions. The action plan comes at the very end.

mcqs.q: In compromising, both parties:
options: Give up something and get something
mcqs.why: The correct answer is giving up something and getting something. In this way the problem is settled peacefully without violence. It differs from win-lose, where one side tries to make the other lose.

mcqs.q: For an international conflict like Kashmir, the chapter's activity concludes that the better settlement is:
options: A negotiated and peaceful settlement rather than war
Ignoring the wishes of the people
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a negotiated, peaceful settlement. War only destroys lives and property. Negotiation and mediation can give a lasting solution acceptable to all parties.

lessons.title: History Skills
lessons.notes_html:
Interpretation Skills

To interpret a historical image, study it carefully and list observations: what do you see, and what details stand out? Then write a short paragraph interpreting it — which event or period it represents and what message the creator wanted to convey. The same evidence can be interpreted in more than one way, so historians must check an interpretation against other sources before accepting it.

Sources of Historical Evidence

  • Five sources of historical evidence: diaries, personal letters, memoirs, newspapers and artifacts such as coins, tools and pottery.
  • Diaries, letters and memoirs are primary sources written by people who lived at that time.
  • A personal letter tells us what the writer saw, felt and thought, and gives information about daily life, prices, travel and public events that official records often do not mention.
  • Steps of historical research: find sources of evidence, check the credibility and context of each source, interpret the evidence, and write a balanced narrative of the past.

Dealing with Archival Material

Old documents may have joined and faded handwriting, old spellings and unclear gaps. Historians read them slowly, guess difficult words from the sense of the sentence and use a magnifying glass for faint parts. Historical documents must be preserved because once they are lost, that evidence can never be recovered.

Objectivity Skills

  • An objective summary gives only facts — what happened, where, and what action was taken — without personal feeling.
  • A subjective summary adds the writer's sadness, opinions and judgements.
  • Objectivity makes an account reliable and balanced; subjectivity shows one person's viewpoint.

Activities from the Chapter

  • Interpretation example: the British conquered Sindh in 1843 for control of the Indus trade routes; Sir Charles Napier defeated the Talpur Mirs at the Battle of Miani and annexed Sindh.
  • Archival research example: Sindh was separated from the Bombay Presidency on 1 April 1936 under the Government of India Act 1935; sources include government records, gazette notifications and contemporary newspapers.
  • For the Sama dynasty (1335-1520), sources include Persian chronicles, inscriptions on mosques and tombs of Thatta and Makli, and old coins.
  • For Talpur architecture, sources include the palaces and tombs themselves, inscriptions, old photographs and official survey records.

mcqs.q: In the interpretation exercise, the photograph of the ruins of Mohenjo-Daro shows:
options: Rows of baked-brick houses, straight streets, the Great Bath and covered drains
mcqs.why: The correct answer is baked-brick houses, planned streets, the Great Bath and covered drains. These details show an organized city life about 4,500 years ago. Historians still check such interpretations against other sources.

mcqs.q: Which of these are primary sources of historical evidence?
options: Diaries, personal letters and memoirs written by people who lived at that time
mcqs.why: The correct answer is diaries, letters and memoirs of the time. Newspapers and artifacts such as coins and pottery also give direct evidence. Later textbooks are secondary sources.

mcqs.q: A personal letter is valuable to a historian because it:
options: Gives the final judgement on events
Tells what the writer saw, felt and thought in his or her own words
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that it records the writer's own experience. It can tell about daily life, prices, travel and public events. Official records often do not mention these details.

mcqs.q: The correct order of historical research is:
options: Find sources, check credibility and context, interpret the evidence, write a balanced narrative
Write the story first, then look for sources
mcqs.why: The correct answer follows the chapter's flow of research steps. Credibility and context must be checked before interpretation. Only then can a balanced narrative of the past be written.

mcqs.q: While transcribing a faded handwritten letter, a historian can overcome difficulties by:
options: Reading slowly, guessing difficult words from the sense of the sentence and using a magnifying glass
Rewriting the letter in new words
mcqs.why: The correct answer is slow reading, sense-based guessing and a magnifying glass. These are the same careful methods used with real archival material. Guessing is guided by the sentence, not invented freely.

mcqs.q: Historical documents must be preserved because:
options: They are valuable only for decoration
They can be sold for high prices
Once lost, that evidence can never be recovered
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that lost evidence cannot be recovered. Archives keep the record of events, people and daily life safe. Future generations then learn true history from original sources.

mcqs.q: An objective summary of an event contains:
options: Only facts, without personal opinion or bias
mcqs.why: The correct answer is facts only. Objectivity makes an account reliable and balanced. Adding feelings and opinions makes a summary subjective.

mcqs.q: A subjective summary differs from an objective one because it:
options: Includes the writer's perspective and feelings about the event
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that it includes personal perspective and feelings. Subjectivity shows one person's viewpoint and may mislead if not separated from facts. Both summaries can describe the same event.

mcqs.q: Sindh was separated from the Bombay Presidency on:
options: 1 April 1936, under the Government of India Act 1935
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1 April 1936 under the Government of India Act 1935. Karachi became the capital of the new province. Sources for this topic are government records, gazette notifications and contemporary newspapers.

mcqs.q: The British annexed Sindh in 1843 after Sir Charles Napier defeated the Talpur Mirs at:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Battle of Miani. Trade, strategy and expansion — not a single cause — explain the conquest. The River Indus was the key route the British wanted to control.

lessons.title: Geographic Skills
lessons.notes_html:
What Is Satellite Imagery?

  • Satellite imagery is used to take photographs of the Earth from space.
  • The basic element of satellite imagery is a pixel; the whole image is arranged in a row-and-column structure of pixels, and each pixel carries information about a small part of the Earth.
  • Satellite images are produced in digital form through line scanners and digital cameras.
  • Comparing past and present images of a town shows change: fields replaced by housing colonies, wider roads and more buildings.
  • The cardinal directions on a map are North, East, South and West.

Three Categories of Satellite Imagery

CategoryFeatures
Visible ImageryCan be viewed only during the day time, when clouds reflect the light of the sun
Infrared ImageryCan be viewed at any point of the day; measures the heat radiating from the sun
Water Vapour ImageryMeasures the amount of water vapour present in the atmosphere

Who Uses Satellite Imagery and Why

  • Geographers use it for mapping the use of land and studying changes in land use over time.
  • Oceanographers use it to assess the condition of the sea — temperature, currents and the movement of fish.
  • Meteorologists use it to forecast the behaviour of the atmosphere.
  • Agrologists use it to see crop yield and crop patterns; foresters use it for identification of vegetation density and conservation of wildlife.
  • Media companies use it to show how a natural disaster has affected a country or region.
  • Governments use it for town planning, monitoring borders and managing natural disasters; businessmen use it to select suitable sites for shops, factories and farms.

Maps and Satellite Imagery

A map gives recorded information such as boundaries, capitals, districts, rivers and mountain peaks in symbols — it tells us where things are. Satellite imagery gives a real and recent view from space — it tells us what is happening there at present. Together they give complete geographical information.

mcqs.q: Satellite imagery is used to take photographs of ______ from space.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Earth. Satellites photograph the Earth's surface from space. Geographers use these images for mapping land use.

mcqs.q: The three categories of satellite imagery are Visible Imagery, Infrared Imagery and ______ Imagery.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Water Vapour Imagery. Visible imagery works only in daytime, and infrared imagery measures heat. Water vapour imagery measures the moisture in the atmosphere.

mcqs.q: Satellite imagery is used by meteorologists to forecast the behaviour of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the atmosphere. Weather forecasting depends on watching clouds, heat and water vapour from space. This warns people about rains, storms and floods in advance.

mcqs.q: The basic element of satellite imagery is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a pixel. The whole image is arranged in rows and columns of pixels. Each pixel carries the information of a small part of the Earth.

mcqs.q: Geographers use satellite imagery for:
options: Mapping the use of land and studying changes in land use over time
mcqs.why: The correct answer is mapping land use. From above, geographers can see towns, roads, forests and cultivated areas. They can then prepare accurate maps and study changes over time.

mcqs.q: Oceanographers use satellite imagery to:
options: Assess the condition of the sea, including temperature, currents and movement of fish
mcqs.why: The correct answer is assessing the condition of the sea. This information is useful for ships, fishermen and weather experts. Foresters, in contrast, watch vegetation density and wildlife.

mcqs.q: Visible Imagery can be viewed:
options: At any point of the day
Only during the day time, when clouds reflect the light of the sun
mcqs.why: The correct answer is only during the day time. Infrared imagery can be viewed at any point of the day because it measures heat. Visible imagery depends on reflected sunlight.

mcqs.q: Infrared Imagery measures:
options: The heat radiating from the sun
mcqs.why: The correct answer is heat. That is why it works day and night. Water vapour imagery is the category that measures moisture in the atmosphere.

mcqs.q: Media companies use satellite imagery to:
options: Show how a natural disaster may have affected a country or region
mcqs.why: The correct answer is showing the effects of natural disasters. Images of floods, earthquakes or storms make reports clear and believable. They also help governments and relief agencies decide where help is needed most.

mcqs.q: A map and satellite imagery differ because:
options: A map tells where things are, while satellite imagery shows what is happening there at present
Both give exactly the same information
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that maps give recorded information in symbols, while satellite imagery gives a real, recent view. Together they give complete geographical information. Neither replaces the other fully.

lessons.title: Mapping Skills for Study of Urbanization in Pakistan
lessons.notes_html:
What Is Urbanization?

Urbanization is the movement of people from villages to cities, where economic activities are centered around non-agricultural occupations such as trade, manufacturing industry and management. As more and more people settle in cities, the cities grow in size and population. In Pakistan this process has been continuing rapidly since independence.

Key Statistics from the Chapter

FactFigure
Urban population of Pakistan, 199843 million
Urban population of Pakistan, 2017Around 76 million
Definition of an urban centre (1998 census)A place with 5,000 or more people
Roots of early city growth in South AsiaAround 5,500 years back
Rural population expected to equal urban population byThe year 2030

Change in Urbanization 1998-2017 (urban share)

RegionChange
Sindh48.75% to 52.02%
Punjab31.27% to 36.71%
Baluchistan23.89% to 27.55%
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa16.87% to 18.77%
PakistanFrom 43 million to 76 million people

Reasons and Patterns

  • Three main reasons of urbanization in Pakistan: refugees settled in cities after independence; industrialization drew people to cities for better jobs and wages; cities offer better educational and health facilities while rural living standards are poor.
  • Patterns of urbanization are categorized in terms of demographic aspects, economic aspects and social aspects.
  • Trade is the buying and selling of goods and services; its types are internal (wholesale and retail) and external (import, export and entrepot) trade.
  • On a population map, densely populated places are the big cities of Sindh and Punjab along rivers and roads, while Baluchistan, the Thar desert and the northern mountains are sparsely populated.

mcqs.q: Around how many people live in urban areas of Pakistan according to the census of 2017?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is around 76 million. In 1998 the urban population was 43 million. The increase shows urbanization is rapid and continuous in Pakistan.

mcqs.q: According to the 1998 census definition, an urban centre is a place with ______ or more people.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 5,000 or more people. This was the official definition used in the 1998 census statistics. Places below this size were counted as rural.

mcqs.q: Patterns of urbanization are categorized in demographic, economic and ______ aspects.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is social aspects. Together, the demographic, economic and social aspects describe the pattern of urbanization. Each aspect shows a different side of city growth.

mcqs.q: Archaeologists and historians consider the roots of early city growth in South Asia to be around ______ years back.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is around 5,500 years. This takes us back to the age of the Indus Valley cities. Urban life in this region is therefore very ancient.

mcqs.q: The rural population is expected to equal the urban population by the year:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 2030. The chapter gives this expectation from the census trends. It shows how fast cities are growing compared with villages.

mcqs.q: Urbanization is:
options: The movement of people from cities to villages
The building of dams on rivers
The movement of people from villages to cities where non-agricultural occupations are centred
The growth of forests near cities
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the movement of people from villages to cities. In cities, activities centre on trade, manufacturing and management. In Pakistan this process has continued rapidly since independence.

mcqs.q: One main reason of urbanization in Pakistan is:
options: Industrialization made people shift to cities in search of better jobs and wage rates
mcqs.why: The correct answer is industrialization drawing people for jobs and wages. Refugees settling in cities after independence was another reason. Better education and health facilities in cities also attract people.

mcqs.q: Which province's urban share rose from 48.75% to 52.02% between 1998 and 2017?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Sindh. It has the highest urban share because of Karachi. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa rose the least, from 16.87% to 18.77%.

mcqs.q: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's urban share changed from:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 16.87% to 18.77%. It is the smallest increase among the provinces. Punjab rose from 31.27% to 36.71% and Baluchistan from 23.89% to 27.55%.

mcqs.q: Trade has two main types — internal and external. Internal trade is divided into:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is wholesale and retail trade. External trade is divided into import, export and entrepot trade. Trade is one of the main activities around which cities grow.
